title: Implement refund and reversal confirmation
description:
## Objective
Create one attributable full-refund relationship for an eligible original transaction and reject partial, over-refund, unmatched, duplicate-role, and incompatible attempts without changing existing state.

## Implements
- FR-LEDGER-REFUND-CONFIRMATION: Confirm refunds and reversals
- DD-LEDGER-FULL-AMOUNT-REFUND-RELATIONSHIP: Single full-amount refund relationships
- DD-LEDGER-IMMUTABLE-HISTORY: Immutable facts and append-only history

## Depends On
- bd-xq6: closed; provides RelationshipStore and active-role model
- bd-2ne: closed; provides LedgerMutationExecutor
- bd-84s: closed; provides TransactionStore

## In Scope
- Publish ledger.refund.confirm through the typed CLI contract.
- Require active same-account ZAR transactions with original amount below zero, refund amount above zero, and exact absolute minor-unit equality.
- Store one immutable refund relationship with refund_original and refund_credit roles.
- Reject partial, over-refund, missing, incompatible, inactive, and active-role duplicate attempts atomically.
- Preserve idempotent request and logical-effect replay.
- Verify source immutability and relationship detail/history.

## Out of Scope
- Partial or cumulative refunds.
- Relationship revoke/replace and actuals projection, which remain downstream tasks.
- Any migration or weakening of financial_relationship_roles_are_exclusive_before_insert.
- Inference from descriptions, dates, category, pool, instrument, cardholder, or evidence.

## Interfaces
- Produces: RefundOperationModule and RefundPolicy
- Consumes: RelationshipStore, TransactionStore, LedgerMutationExecutor.ExecuteAsync

## Files
- src/Tally/Contracts/Ledger/Relationships/RefundContracts.cs (create)
- src/Tally/Domain/Ledger/Relationships/RefundPolicy.cs (create)
- src/Tally/Features/Ledger/Relationships/RefundHandlers.cs (create)
- src/Tally/Features/Ledger/Relationships/RefundOperationModule.cs (create)
- src/Tally/Contracts/Common/ProcessContracts.cs (modify)
- src/Tally/Bootstrap/LedgerServices.cs (modify)
- src/Tally/Cli/OperationRegistry.cs (modify)
- src/Tally/Cli/TallyProcess.cs (modify)
- tests/Tally.Tests/Features/Ledger/Relationships/RefundTests.cs (test)

## Verification
- focused RefundTests
- dotnet build
- dotnet test

## Commit
- feat(ledger): implement full-amount refund confirmation
- Refs: bd-10w

## Context
- lex context bd-10w --json
design: Implement a refund-specific typed input, pure RefundPolicy, transactional confirmation handler, and operation module following the existing transfer vertical slice. RefundPolicy returns stable validation codes for input, lifecycle, account, currency, sign, and exact full-amount eligibility. The handler uses the existing RelationshipStore active-role check and V001 exclusivity trigger unchanged, stores the full positive minor-unit amount, and delegates replay to LedgerMutationExecutor.
acceptance_criteria:
- Exact same-account ZAR negative-original and positive-refund amounts create one active full-amount relationship.
- Smaller partial and larger over-refund credits return LEDGER-REFUND-AMOUNT with no relationship or idempotency record.
- Missing, inactive, different-account, different-currency, invalid-sign, invalid-input, and active-role reuse cases return stable errors without mutation.
- A second active refund for an original returns LEDGER-RELATIONSHIP-ACTIVE-ROLE-CONFLICT; the existing relationship remains the only active one.
- Identical request and logical-effect replay return the original relationship; changed input under one key returns LEDGER-IDEMPOTENCY-001.
- Detail exposes exact roles, amount, currency, active state, actor, time, and history; both source transactions remain unchanged.
- The existing V001 relationship-role exclusivity trigger and RelationshipStore guard are unchanged.
- Focused RefundTests run at least 16 cases with zero failures; full build and test gates pass.
notes: Resolved product correction: Ledger supports one exact full refund only. Existing role-exclusivity trigger and RelationshipStore semantics were verified correct and remain unchanged. Graph design/plan/task contracts were corrected and documentation review converged. Implementation commit e14542ef305f05602500037a8ca61e60362b0ac4 passes RefundTests 27/27, full suite 547/547, build with 0 warnings/errors, format verification, linux-x64 Native AOT publish, and typed published-schema inspection. Self-review PASS for spec conformance and code quality; durable report: docs/reviews/review-work-ledger-refunds-2026-07-22.md; Lex verification record 01KY4734YKSPS2EZCBZX3SM342.

title: Verify failure handling and cleanup workflow
description:
## Objective

Prove an owner can recover from or safely terminate every failed ingestion without payload disclosure, source damage, or Ledger deletion.

## Implements

- No direct FR; this task is a prerequisite or verification gate.

## Depends On

- bd-2jn (TASK-INGEST-GATE-INT-PUBLIC-CONTRACT): UC verification exercises published status/abandon/cleanup operations.
- bd-114 (TASK-INGEST-GATE-SECURITY): The workflow consumes the consolidated security canary and permission evidence.

## In Scope

- UCIngest005Evidence

## Out of Scope

- Do NOT inspect/delete files directly from the test except through isolated setup/observation helpers; invoke public abandon/cleanup for behavior.
- Do NOT emit private payload when a case fails.

## Success Criteria

- Every failure returns stable code/category, batchId and candidateId when each identity has been created and is available, mutation possibility, last durable state, and retry/resume/abandon/correct-source guidance with one stdout result and metadata-only stderr.
- When payload would be needed to explain an error, the result uses every available batchId, candidateId, and sourceRecordId instead and canary data is absent from every output/log; a pre-identity failure does not fabricate an unavailable identifier.
- Permission-establishment failure persists no sensitive artifact and performs no Ledger mutation.
- Status proves pre-commit failures have no committable manifest/effect and commit-stage failures preserve exact completed outcomes plus unresolved frontier.
- A simulated crash leaves only known durable/recoverable artifacts; next startup after acquiring the artifact-cleanup lock removes disposable residue and retains required state.
- Cleanup rejects ambiguous/locked/recoverable targets; abandon prevents commit/resume but preserves prior effects; terminal cleanup removes only selected INGEST artifacts and leaves source/Ledger unchanged.

## Failure Criteria

- ❌ Do NOT inspect/delete files directly from the test except through isolated setup/observation helpers; invoke public abandon/cleanup for behavior.
- ❌ Do NOT emit private payload when a case fails.
## Approach

Black-box use-case gate for UC-INGEST-005 diagnostics, durable status, retry/resume/abandon decisions, and state-checked cleanup.

Constraints:
- Filesystem observations are restricted to isolated test data roots and source hashes; cleanup never targets the repository fixture directory.

## Interfaces

- Consumes: CompleteIngestPublicContract (DM-INGEST-OPERATION-CONTRACTS)
- Consumes: IngestSecurityGateEvidence (NFR-INGEST-LOCAL-DATA-PROTECTION)
- Produces: UCIngest005Evidence (UC-INGEST-005)

title: Enforce ancestry, overflow, sign, and lifecycle integrity during envelope resolution
description:
## Objective
Malformed frozen ancestry and Int64 overflow return the stable integrity failure with no partial result, while refund-negative amounts and archived ancestors resolve without reclassification.

## Implements
- FR-BUDGET-CATEGORY-LIFECYCLE: Honor Spend Category lifecycle
  - AC: Given plan validation, when BUDGET resolves a Spend Category, then it uses the versioned public LEDGER category contract and the stable category identifier rather than a display name.
- FR-BUDGET-POSITION-QUERY: Calculate exact Budget Positions
  - AC: Given a Budget Actual member whose frozen Spend Category ancestry is empty for a categorized member, does not end with the assigned Spend Category identifier, repeats an identifier, or names an identifier absent from the known Spend Category evidence, when the position is calculated, then BUDGET returns the stable integrity failure and no partial totals.

## Depends On
- bd-3uzt (TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-RESOLUTION): Integrity validation guards the resolution path and shares its ancestry scan.
- bd-1xlf (TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-CONTRACTS): Ancestry validation reads BudgetActualMember.AncestryIds, which that bead adds to the record.

## In Scope
- Ancestry validation mirroring the LEDGER ActualsCalculator invariant
- Checked Int64 overflow across the absorbed-sum path
- Refund-sign preservation and archived-ancestor capture proven by test

## Out of Scope
- The resolution scan itself — bd-3uzt (TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-RESOLUTION)
- Published-contract provenance proofs — bd-zsby (TASK-BUDGET-GATE-INT-ENVELOPE-PROVENANCE)

## Success Criteria
- Given a categorized member whose ancestry is empty, does not end with its assigned Spend Category identifier, repeats an identifier, or names an identifier absent from known Spend Category evidence, when the position is calculated, then BudgetErrors.Integrity is returned with an amount-free integrity reason token and no position row or totals.
- Given an uncategorized member whose ancestry list is non-empty, when the position is calculated, then BudgetErrors.Integrity is returned with no partial totals.
- Given descendant Budget Actuals whose absorbed sum exceeds Int64 range, when the position is calculated, then BudgetErrors.Integrity is returned, no position row or totals are produced, and no amount appears in the failure message.
- Given a parent Category Budget Entry and descendant Budget Actuals whose signed sum is negative because refunds exceed spend, when the position is returned, then the exact negative value is preserved in both the descendant actual and the row actual, the row stays in the Budgeted bucket, and the membership reconciliation assertion still holds.
- Given an archived ancestor Spend Category carrying a Category Budget Entry and an active descendant carrying none, when the position is calculated, then the archived ancestor row absorbs the descendant Budget Actuals exactly once and reports its archived lifecycle.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do NOT clamp, zero, or reclassify a negative Budget Actual — refund-heavy negatives stay signed, per DD-BUDGET-CATEGORY-ENVELOPE-RESOLUTION.
- ❌ Do NOT skip an archived ancestor during resolution — Spend Category lifecycle never changes bucket assignment, per DD-BUDGET-CATEGORY-ENVELOPE-RESOLUTION.
- ❌ Do NOT return a partial position, partial totals, or a best-effort row when integrity fails — per DD-BUDGET-EXACT-POSITION-CALCULATION overflow yields a stable integrity failure with no partial result.
- ❌ Do NOT include any monetary amount in an integrity failure message or reason token — amount-free diagnostics only.

## Approach
- Integrity failures use the existing BudgetErrors.Integrity code and the existing amount-free reason-token mechanism.
- No new error code is introduced for ancestry violations.

Expected outputs:
- Ancestry validation mirroring the LEDGER ActualsCalculator invariant
- Checked Int64 overflow handling across the absorbed-sum path
- Archived-ancestor and refund-sign behavior proven by test

## Interfaces
- Consumes: BudgetActualMember.AncestryIds (DM-BUDGET-POSITION-PROJECTION) — Validated here; field declared by TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-CONTRACTS
- Produces: BudgetPositionCalculator.TryGetIntegrityReason (DM-BUDGET-POSITION-PROJECTION) — Amount-free integrity reason token accessor

## Files (reservation globs)
- `src/Tally/Domain/Budget/Position/BudgetPositionCalculator.cs` (modify)
- `tests/Tally.Tests/Budget/Position/BudgetEnvelopeIntegrityTests.cs` (create)

## Verification
- **Build:** `dotnet build Tally.slnx --nologo` — Build succeeded with 0 errors and 0 warnings
- **Test:** `dotnet test tests/Tally.Tests/Tally.Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~BudgetEnvelopeIntegrityTests` — All BudgetEnvelopeIntegrityTests pass, exit code 0, at least 5 tests run

## Commit
- `feat(budget): validate ancestry and overflow during envelope resolution` — one commit for this bead; footer line `Refs: bd-113k`

## Lex references
- TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-INTEGRITY, FR-BUDGET-CATEGORY-LIFECYCLE, FR-BUDGET-POSITION-QUERY, DD-BUDGET-CATEGORY-ENVELOPE-RESOLUTION, NFR-BUDGET-EXACT-FINANCIAL-INTEGRITY
- Deep context: `lex context bd-113k --json`

## Objective
GetInsightReportQuery and ExplainInsightReportQuery return only the selected immutable stored evidence without recomputing current producers or mutating history.

## Implements
- FR-INSIGHTS-REPORT-EXPLANATION: Explain report evidence deterministically
  - AC: Given a supported exact metric, when its explanation is inspected, then exact value, window bounds, category or total identity, source evidence references, and arithmetic rule are returned.
  - AC: Given a supported Linear Pace state, when its explanation is inspected, then formula version, elapsed and total days, exact plan and actual inputs, exact comparison result, and uniform-distribution limitation are returned.
  - AC: Given an unavailable, insufficient, not-started, or deferred state, when its explanation is inspected, then the typed reason, evaluated evidence, unmet rule, and permitted next action are returned without an invented result.
  - AC: Given a retained Report Snapshot identity, when Get or Explain is requested, then the exact immutable stored explanation and provenance are returned rather than recomputing current evidence.
  - AC: Given an unknown retained identity, when Get or Explain is requested, then Not Found is returned without leaking other report metadata.
  - AC: Given a deleted retained identity with a Deletion Event, when Get or Explain is requested, then Deleted is returned with metadata-only deletion evidence and no prior report payload.
  - AC: Given explanatory text, when it is compared across identical structured states and policy versions, then it is semantically identical, template-based, channel-neutral, and contains no persuasion, recommendation, translation, or delivery wording.
- FR-INSIGHTS-REPORT-HISTORY: Inspect retained report history and status

  - AC: Given an unknown retained identity, when Get is requested, then Not Found is returned without other report metadata.

  - AC: Given retained history, when List ordering is inspected, then it is trusted creation time descending followed by stable report identity descending.
  - AC: Given a List request over the released count or output limit, when it is validated, then resource failure is returned rather than silent truncation.

## Objective

title: Generate one ephemeral Insight Report
description:
## Objective
GenerateInsightReportQuery returns one bounded complete report from one frozen instant and one coherent producer result while changing no durable state.

## Implements
- FR-INSIGHTS-REPORT-GENERATION: Generate one deterministic Insight Report
  - AC: Given a valid generation request and coherent evidence, when generation succeeds, then exactly one ephemeral Insight Report is returned and no durable INSIGHTS state changes.
  - AC: Given omitted optional policy selectors, when generation succeeds, then the released default window, formula, Evidence Sufficiency, explanation, and ordering versions are explicit in the result.
  - AC: Given one report, when its content is inspected, then report identity, Budget Period, trusted As-of Instant, exact windows, plan state, exact metrics, every requested signal state, limitations, and Source Provenance are present.
  - AC: Given identical trusted As-of Instant, normalized request values, coherent source identities, and policy versions, when generation is repeated, then semantically identical ordered content and the same content fingerprint are returned.
  - AC: Given categories, metrics, states, and explanations, when report ordering is inspected, then it follows the released deterministic ordering policy and never depends on localized display text.
  - AC: Given one report, when Source Provenance is inspected, then all producer contract versions, authoritative state or snapshot identities, plan revision, category contract, report schema, policy versions, and content fingerprints are present.
  - AC: Given a requested horizon, category count, metric count, or output size over a released limit, when validation occurs, then resource failure is returned before producer reads or report output.
  - AC: Given a successful report, when its claims are inspected, then it describes recorded Tally evidence and does not claim complete bank activity, financial advice, enforcement, or historical source reconstruction.
- FR-INSIGHTS-STRUCTURED-INVOCATION: Invoke Public INSIGHTS Operations non-interactively
  - AC: Given valid structured input through stdin or an approved owner-only file, when a public operation succeeds, then exactly one versioned structured business-result envelope is written to stdout and the process exits with the documented success category.
  - AC: Given an expected validation, Not Found, Deleted, conflict, unavailable, insufficient-evidence, compatibility, integrity, resource, or downstream failure, when invocation completes, then exactly one module-scoped machine-readable error or state envelope is returned with the documented exit category.
  - AC: Given malformed input or a schema-forbidden unknown field, when invocation is attempted, then validation fails before any financial read or retained-state write.
  - AC: Given an unsupported INSIGHTS, BUDGET, or LEDGER contract version, when invocation is attempted, then compatibility fails before financial processing.
  - AC: Given Retain, Restate, Delete, Backup, or Restore without required P1 actor attribution or idempotency identity, when invocation is attempted, then authority validation fails before retained-state change.
  - AC: Given any operation, when it runs, then it requires no interactive prompt, network call, daemon, watcher, scheduler, service, or background Tally process.
  - AC: Given success or expected failure, when stderr, logs, telemetry, crash output, process arguments, and shared temporary locations are inspected, then they contain metadata only and no serialized financial request, report, or response body.

## Depends On
- bd-uh9 (TASK-INSIGHTS-CONTRACT-FOUNDATION): The query implements a published request/result and stable error contract.
- bd-388 (TASK-INSIGHTS-BUDGET-EVIDENCE-CLIENT): Generation consumes the single public BUDGET client.
- bd-3ac (TASK-INSIGHTS-REPORT-COMPILER): Generation delegates all analytical semantics to the compiler.

## In Scope
- Implement the read-only Generate vertical slice from validated structured request through one BUDGET call and deterministic compilation.
- Produce: GenerateInsightReportQuery
- Produce: Ephemeral generation contract tests

## Out of Scope
- No sibling handoff beyond the explicit Depends On and Failure Criteria contracts.

## Success Criteria
- Generate validates unknown fields, versions, requested policies, rolling windows, category/metric/signal counts, horizon, and output bounds before TimeProvider or producer access.
- A valid request freezes TimeProvider.GetUtcNow exactly once before calling BudgetContractClient.GetInsightEvidenceAsync exactly once, binds the result, and compiles one complete InsightReport.
- Omitted selectors resolve to explicit released default window, formula, sufficiency, explanation, and ordering versions in the result.
- Success writes no ReportSnapshot, idempotency record, recovery metadata, file, or store state; expected failure returns one typed envelope and no partial report.
- CancellationToken is forwarded through every async call and logs contain only operation identity, correlation reference, duration, safe fingerprints, states, and counts.

title: Validate built-in policies with private owner evidence
description:
## Objective
Changed built-in policies can enter the released catalogue only after complete owner-only cases, canaries, aggregate outcomes, and owner acceptance pass without private disclosure.

## Implements
- FR-INSIGHTS-PRIVATE-POLICY-VALIDATION: Validate analytical policies against private evidence
  - AC: Given a candidate policy set and owner-only evaluation manifest, when validation starts, then candidate versions, expected-state fingerprint, corpus fingerprint, producer contract versions, window policy, and evaluation-tool version are recorded.
  - AC: Given a completed validation run, when its result is returned, then every manifest case is accounted for as supported, unavailable, insufficient, correct signal, incorrect signal, correct severity, false severity, or disclosure-canary outcome.
  - AC: Given sparse, zero, recurring, front-loaded, irregular, refund-heavy, plan-change, category-lifecycle, classification-gap, and correction cases, when required corpus coverage is checked, then every required shape is present or validation fails before policy activation.
  - AC: Given any false high-severity Attention Item, when candidate activation is evaluated, then the Attention Item policy is rejected.
  - AC: Given a candidate Forecast, Trend, or Anomaly without a deterministic formula, explicit comparable baseline, minimum evidence rule, limitations, and named unavailable state, when activation is evaluated, then that signal policy is rejected.
  - AC: Given a candidate report shape that the owner does not accept as improving a named decision over raw Budget Position inspection, when the plan gate is evaluated, then the do-less kill criterion is reported as triggered.
  - AC: Given an unavailable private manifest, when existing released policies are used, then ordinary report generation may continue with their unchanged versions.
  - AC: Given an unavailable private manifest, when a new or changed analytical policy is proposed for release, then activation is blocked.
  - AC: Given a validation result, when it is persisted or exported, then only fingerprints, structural case identifiers, aggregate outcomes, and canary status are present; filenames, financial values, merchant text, report payloads, and expected rows are absent.
  - AC: Given the public INSIGHTS capability set, when it is enumerated, then no owner-facing policy create, edit, activate, retire, scripting, or plugin operation is present; candidate validation is a release evidence gate for built-in policies.

## Depends On
- bd-uh9 (TASK-INSIGHTS-CONTRACT-FOUNDATION): The harness validates released catalogue and receipt contracts.
- bd-3ac (TASK-INSIGHTS-REPORT-COMPILER): Private cases exercise the real candidate compiler rather than a second evaluator.
- bd-21u (TASK-INSIGHTS-LIFECYCLE-CONTRACT-MODELS): The private harness emits the external aggregate PolicyValidationReceipt.

## In Scope
- Implement the internal manifest-driven validation harness and privacy-safe external receipt for active built-in policies and candidate report shape.
- Produce: InsightPolicyValidationHarness
- Produce: PrivateEvaluationManifestReader
- Produce: PolicyValidationReceiptWriter
- Produce: Privacy and coverage tests

## Out of Scope
- The durable receipt is release/test evidence outside active product state; private cases remain ignored and owner-controlled.

## Success Criteria
- InsightPolicyValidationHarness accepts the private manifest only from TALLY_INSIGHTS_PRIVATE_EVALUATION_MANIFEST, requires an owner-only regular file, and reads cases in memory without printing paths or payloads.
- Validation records candidate policy, report schema, producer contract, window, corpus, expected-state, and tool fingerprints and accounts for every structural case as supported, unavailable, insufficient, correct/incorrect signal, correct/false severity, or disclosure-canary outcome.
- Sparse, zero, recurring, front-loaded, irregular, refund-heavy, plan-change, category-lifecycle, classification-gap, correction, false-severity, and disclosure-canary shapes are required before success.
- The external PolicyValidationReceipt contains only approved structural IDs, fingerprints, aggregate outcomes, false-high-severity count, canary status, tool version, and owner acceptance; it is never inserted into insights.db.
- Missing evidence blocks changed policy release but does not disable unchanged released policies; deferred policies remain non-executable.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do NOT add a public validation, policy CRUD, expression, script, plugin, activation, or retirement operation — rejected per DD-INSIGHTS-PRIVATE-POLICY-VALIDATION.
- ❌ Do NOT commit anonymized private examples or rely on synthetic tests alone — rejected per DD-INSIGHTS-PRIVATE-POLICY-VALIDATION.
- ❌ Do NOT persist manifest paths, filenames, financial values, merchant text, report payloads, expected rows, corpus rows, or PolicyValidationReceipt in the active store.
- ❌ Do NOT release a changed policy when any case, required shape, disclosure canary, owner acceptance, or zero-false-high-severity gate is absent or failing.

## Approach
Implement the internal manifest-driven validation harness and privacy-safe external receipt for active built-in policies and candidate report shape.
- Constraint: Ordinary report generation must not require the private corpus for unchanged released policy versions.
- Expected output: InsightPolicyValidationHarness
- Expected output: PrivateEvaluationManifestReader
- Expected output: PolicyValidationReceiptWriter
- Expected output: Privacy and coverage tests

## Interfaces
- Consumes: InsightReportCompiler.Compile (DM-INSIGHTS-INSIGHT-REPORT) — real candidate compiler
- Consumes: PolicyValidationReceipt (DM-INSIGHTS-POLICY-VALIDATION-RECEIPT) — external aggregate release evidence
- Produces: InsightPolicyValidationHarness.ValidateAsync (DM-INSIGHTS-POLICY-VALIDATION-RECEIPT) — complete private case evaluation
- Produces: PolicyValidationReceiptWriter.WriteAsync (DM-INSIGHTS-POLICY-VALIDATION-RECEIPT) — owner-only aggregate receipt writer

## Files (reservation globs)
- `src/Tally/Features/Insights/PolicyValidation/PrivateEvaluationManifestReader.cs` (create) — owner-only manifest boundary
- `src/Tally/Features/Insights/PolicyValidation/InsightPolicyValidationHarness.cs` (create) — complete case and canary evaluator
- `src/Tally/Features/Insights/PolicyValidation/PolicyValidationReceiptWriter.cs` (create) — aggregate external receipt writer

## Verification

title: Restore through a verified generation and atomic activation
description:
## Objective
RestoreInsightsBackupCommand activates either one complete verified restored generation or leaves the prior authoritative generation unchanged under every fault.

## Implements
- FR-INSIGHTS-BACKUP-VERIFY-RESTORE: Back up, verify, and restore retained INSIGHTS state
  - AC: Given a valid owner-only backup target, when Backup succeeds, then all durable Report Snapshots, Restatement links, Deletion Events, idempotency outcomes, policy metadata, and storage-version evidence are captured in one attributable point-in-time artifact.
  - AC: Given Backup, when its contents are inspected, then ephemeral producer cursors, temporary reports, private evaluation rows, raw merchant text, and unrelated upstream state are absent.
  - AC: Given a backup artifact, when Verify succeeds, then cryptographic fingerprint, format and storage compatibility, ownership and permissions, complete counts, link integrity, content fingerprints, idempotency outcomes, and deletion-state consistency are independently checked.
  - AC: Given corruption, omission, incompatible version, unsafe ownership or permissions, or failed integrity, when Verify runs, then the exact failure is returned and no active store changes.
  - AC: Given a verified compatible backup, when Restore starts, then it builds and validates a separate candidate without modifying the active store.
  - AC: Given a complete verified candidate, when Restore activates, then the selected backup state becomes authoritative atomically and the prior store remains available until activation succeeds.
  - AC: Given cancellation, crash, insufficient space, permission failure, or migration failure before activation, when recovery completes, then the prior authoritative store is unchanged.
  - AC: Given a backup created before a later report deletion, when that backup is explicitly restored, then its exact captured report and deletion state are reinstated and identified in the restore result.

## Depends On
- bd-2bm (TASK-INSIGHTS-BACKUP-VERIFY): Restore reuses the independent artifact verifier.
- bd-7kn (TASK-INSIGHTS-STATE-FOUNDATION): Restore uses generation layout, migrations, integrity, and writer coordination.
- bd-2nv (TASK-INSIGHTS-IDEMPOTENCY-EXECUTOR): Restore records and replays one outcome inside the activated candidate.

## In Scope
- Implement source verification, separate generation construction, compatible migration, restore outcome recording, revalidation, expected-current locking, and atomic CURRENT replacement.
- Produce: InsightsRestoreActivator
- Produce: RestoreInsightsBackupCommand
- Produce: Atomic activation fault tests

## Out of Scope
- No sibling handoff beyond the explicit Depends On and Failure Criteria contracts.

## Success Criteria
- Restore requires source, expected current generation fingerprint, actor, safe path identity, and idempotency and resolves an exact prior outcome before source work.
- The source is independently verified before a separate new generation is created; only compatible ordered migrations run against the candidate, and complete logical, fingerprint, permission, and integrity verification follows.
- The candidate records exactly the current Restore replay outcome and recovery event, is flushed and reverified, then activation acquires the exclusive module writer lock and compares expected current fingerprint before changing authority.
- Successful activation atomically replaces CURRENT and fsyncs its directory; startup observes either the complete old or complete new generation, Status cites durable Restore verification, and the prior generation remains a recovery point.
- Corruption, omission, incompatibility, permission, space, cancellation, migration, verification, expected-current drift, pointer replacement, or fsync failure before completed activation leaves the prior authoritative store unchanged and returns an exact stable failure.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do NOT restore over the live database or rename individual database/WAL files — rejected per DD-INSIGHTS-VERIFIED-RECOVERY-ACTIVATION.
- ❌ Do NOT activate before full candidate verification, skip expected-current revalidation, overwrite the prior generation, persist standalone Verify, or add source business data beyond the captured backup.
- ❌ Do NOT include candidate paths or report payloads in results, diagnostics, logs, or crash output.

## Approach
Implement source verification, separate generation construction, compatible migration, restore outcome recording, revalidation, expected-current locking, and atomic CURRENT replacement.
- Constraint: Only CURRENT is the authority switch; directory fsync and exclusive writer coordination are mandatory.
- Expected output: InsightsRestoreActivator
- Expected output: RestoreInsightsBackupCommand
- Expected output: Atomic activation fault tests

## Interfaces
- Consumes: InsightsBackupVerifier.VerifyAsync (DM-INSIGHTS-RECOVERY-CONTRACTS) — source and candidate verification
- Consumes: InsightsMigrations.ApplyAsync (DM-INSIGHTS-STATE-STORE) — compatible candidate migrations
- Consumes: InsightsIdempotencyExecutor.ExecuteAsync (DM-INSIGHTS-IDEMPOTENCY) — exact replay and Restore outcome
- Produces: InsightsRestoreActivator.ActivateAsync (DM-INSIGHTS-RECOVERY-CONTRACTS) — verified atomic generation activation
- Produces: RestoreInsightsBackupCommand.HandleAsync (DM-INSIGHTS-OPERATION-CONTRACTS) — insights.restore.activate handler

## Files (reservation globs)

- `src/Tally/Features/Insights/Recovery/Restore/RestoreInsightsBackupCommand.cs` (create) — idempotent Restore handler
- `tests/Tally.Tests/Insights/Recovery/InsightsRestoreActivationTests.cs` (test) — source, migration, expected-current, atomic pointer, restart, and fault tests

## Verification
- **Build:** `dotnet build`
- **Test:** `dotnet test tests/Tally.Tests/Tally.Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~InsightsRestoreActivationTests` — exit 0; at least 24 exact-replay, source-verification, incompatible-version, migration, candidate-outcome, revalidation, permission, space, cancellation, expected-current-drift, lock, pointer, fsync, restart-old-or-new, prior-generation, Status, and disclosure cases are discovered and 0 fail

title: Verify agent contract discovery and invocation
description:
## Objective
UC-CLASSIFY-006 proves an AI Agent Host can orchestrate CLASSIFY without prose scraping, private storage, prompts, unrelated data, or bypassed owner intent.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-CONTRACT-DISCOVERY: Discover the CLASSIFY command contract
  - AC: Given a compatible Tally executable, when schema discovery is requested, then the registry exposes every operation required by C12 with its versioned input, result, error, exit, mutability, idempotency, limit, and compatibility contract.
  - AC: Given any public CLASSIFY operation, when its schema is requested repeatedly for the same contract version, then the semantic descriptor is deterministic.
  - AC: Given an unknown CLASSIFY operation, when schema or invocation is requested, then Tally returns a stable unknown-operation error and no private storage detail.
  - AC: Given contract discovery, when descriptors are returned, then no CLASSIFY store, private corpus, or LEDGER data read occurs.
- FR-CLASSIFY-STATE-RETENTION-CLEANUP: Retain attributable state and clean derived artifacts
  - AC: Given an activated rule, apply result, or feedback record, when retention is inspected, then CLASSIFY retains the minimal actor, reason, timestamp, stable references, fingerprints, prior state, and resulting state required for explanation and replay.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path succeeds, when its result is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path returns an expected failure, when its result is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path returns an unexpected handled failure, when its failure is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given an unreferenced draft rule, validation run, or evaluation run, when the owner explicitly abandons it, then it becomes non-activatable and its removable derived payload is deleted without changing active rules or LEDGER.
  - AC: Given a rule version, evaluation, or apply result referenced by active state, Ledger mutation provenance, or feedback, when hard removal is requested, then CLASSIFY rejects removal and requires lifecycle retirement or retained history.
  - AC: Given process startup, when orphan temporary artifacts from a prior crash are found, then CLASSIFY validates ownership and removes only recognized CLASSIFY temporaries before accepting new mutation.
  - AC: Given cleanup completion, when status is requested, then it returns cleanup run ID, policy version, removed artifact count, retained artifact count, and per-kind counts but no removed payload or path.
- FR-CLASSIFY-STATUS-HISTORY: Inspect classification status and history
  - AC: Given a status request, when current rule state is returned, then it identifies the active Rule Set Version and draft, active, retired, and superseded rule versions with rule version ID, Rule Set Version ID, lifecycle state, actor ID, reason code, created-at timestamp, and predecessor or successor IDs.
  - AC: Given a retained validation or evaluation run, when status is requested, then it returns its fingerprint, lifecycle state, aggregate outcome counts, staleness state, and exactly one next-operation enum value without rereading the corpus or LEDGER projection.
  - AC: Given a retained apply run, when status is requested, then it returns the authorized fingerprint, terminal item totals, unresolved frontier, and whether replay or resume is safe.
  - AC: Given retained feedback, when status is requested, then it returns the referenced outcome, decision type, proposal state, actor, reason, and rule versions without reconstructing evidence.
  - AC: Given an unknown status subject, when status is requested, then CLASSIFY returns stable not-found and does not search private payloads heuristically.
  - AC: Given any expected failure, when status is returned, then it identifies whether CLASSIFY or LEDGER mutation may have occurred and returns exactly one permitted next-operation enum value from retry, resume, re-evaluate, correct, abandon, cleanup, or none.
- FR-CLASSIFY-STRUCTURED-INVOCATION: Invoke CLASSIFY operations non-interactively
  - AC: Given valid structured input for a public operation, when invocation completes, then exactly one versioned structured business result is written to stdout and the process exits with the documented category.
  - AC: Given an expected validation, not-found, conflict, lifecycle, stale, compatibility, resource, or downstream LEDGER failure, when invocation completes, then one module-scoped machine-readable error is returned with the documented non-zero exit.
  - AC: Given malformed input or a forbidden unknown field, when invocation is attempted, then validation fails before evaluation, rule-state change, or LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given an unsupported CLASSIFY or required LEDGER contract version, when invocation is attempted, then compatibility fails before financial data read or mutation.
  - AC: Given a mutating rule, feedback, abandon, cleanup, or apply operation, when its request lacks required actor context or idempotency identity, then CLASSIFY rejects it before mutation.
  - AC: Given any successful or expected-failure invocation, when stderr is inspected, then it contains metadata-only diagnostics and no serialized request, result, or financial payload.

## Depends On
- bd-3g6y (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-INT-PUBLIC-CONTRACT): The host consumes the complete published contract.
- bd-3tpm (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-STATUS-WORKFLOW): The host uses safe status for lifecycle orchestration.

## In Scope
Validation-only UC task with no implements refs; it traces UC-CLASSIFY-006 schema discovery, valid invocation, compatibility, malformed input, owner boundary, diagnostics, and status.

- VerifiedClassifyUc006

## Out of Scope
- bd-1yaj (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-GRAPH-QUALITY) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- Do not modify files reserved by sibling beads or implement any capability outside the twelve-operation CLASSIFY v1 surface.

## Success Criteria
- The compatible host discovers exactly twelve deterministic descriptors and invokes every operation through structured stdin or file input with one stdout envelope.
- Unsupported CLASSIFY or Ledger versions reject before data read or mutation; malformed and unknown-field requests return stable validation errors.
- Missing owner identity, non-owner file permissions, group or other permission bits, or missing idempotency rejects mutation before state change.
- Diagnostics contain only correlation ID, operation ID, duration, result code, error code, and aggregate item counts; they contain no descriptions, tokens, rules, amounts, corpus rows, paths, serialized requests, or results.
- Status enables orchestration using only published schemas, subject IDs, lifecycle states, mutation-possibility state, frontier ordinal, aggregate counts, and next-operation enum values without reading CLASSIFY storage or searching private payloads.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do not use a human prompt, TTY scraping, HTTP alias, hidden operation, or direct storage read in the host fixture.
- ❌ Do not omit incompatible, malformed, owner-boundary, permission, or diagnostic failure paths.

## Approach
Validation-only UC task with no implements refs; it traces UC-CLASSIFY-006 schema discovery, valid invocation, compatibility, malformed input, owner boundary, diagnostics, and status.

Constraints:
- Validation-only gate is intentionally loose and uses a compatible local AI Agent Host test client.

- Consumes: GetClassificationStatusQuery.HandleAsync (DM-CLASSIFY-STATE-STORE)
- Produces: VerifiedClassifyUc006 (UC-CLASSIFY-006)

title: Save immutable rule drafts
description:
## Objective
The owner can append a validated-shape rule draft while invalid fields or categories create no activatable state and no Ledger mutation.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-RULE-LIFECYCLE: Manage versioned deterministic rules
  - AC: Given a supported predicate over schema-allowed fields and an active category identifier, when a rule draft is saved, then CLASSIFY records a new immutable draft version with owner, reason, scope, normalization version, and proposed category.
  - AC: Given a rule draft is saved, when the operation completes, then no rule or Rule Set Version is activated and no LEDGER mutation occurs.
  - AC: Given an unsupported field or predicate, when a rule draft is saved, then CLASSIFY returns stable field-level validation errors and creates no activatable version.
  - AC: Given a category identifier is missing from the current catalogue, when a rule draft is saved, then CLASSIFY returns a stable category-not-found error and creates no activatable version.
  - AC: Given a category identifier is archived in the current catalogue, when a rule draft is saved, then CLASSIFY returns a stable category-inactive error and creates no activatable version.
  - AC: Given a draft whose required private validation passed, when the owner explicitly activates it, then CLASSIFY creates a new immutable active Rule Set Version containing the exact activated rule version.
  - AC: Given an active rule, when the owner retires it with a reason, then CLASSIFY creates a new active Rule Set Version without that rule and retains the retired version for inspection.
  - AC: Given an active rule that must be narrowed or replaced, when the owner activates a validated successor, then the successor references the prior version and the prior version becomes retired or superseded without in-place mutation.
  - AC: Given a category rename that preserves the same active category identifier, when rules are inspected, then their category identity is unchanged and their display name resolves to the current catalogue name.
  - AC: Given any owner decision, correction, or feedback event, when the event is recorded, then no rule version or Rule Set Version is activated automatically.
  - AC: Given a draft entered through classify.rule.save, when it is retained, then its immutable rule version records rule_origin=owner_authored and no personal rule value is compiled, seeded, logged, or exported.
  - AC: Given a draft originating from correction feedback, when it is retained, then its immutable rule version records rule_origin=feedback_derived and receives no validation, activation, broad-apply, or mutation authority from that origin.

## Depends On
- bd-2olb (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-LEDGER-CLASSIFICATION-CLIENT): Rule save must validate the target against the current public Ledger category catalogue before persisting an inactive draft.
- bd-3gmq (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-RULE-VOCABULARY): Consumes an interface produced by TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-RULE-VOCABULARY.
- bd-6tql (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-STATE-FOUNDATION): Drafts use the immutable rule and idempotency tables.

## In Scope
Implement rule.save with canonical conditions, current category validation, immutable versions, attribution, and no activation side effect.

- SaveClassificationRuleCommand
- ClassificationRuleStore
- Immutable draft persistence

## Out of Scope
- bd-3g6y (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-INT-PUBLIC-CONTRACT) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- bd-3e6o (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-RULE-ACTIVATION-LIFECYCLE) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- bd-2kpw (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-RULE-VALIDATION) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- Do not modify files reserved by sibling beads or implement any capability outside the twelve-operation CLASSIFY v1 surface.

## Success Criteria
- A supported canonical rule over an active category appends an immutable draft version with owner, reason, scope hash, normalization version, and prior version reference.
- Unsupported fields, predicates, duplicate or empty conditions, invalid values, missing categories, and archived categories return stable field or lifecycle errors and create no activatable version.
- Saving a draft neither changes the active rule-set pointer nor invokes any Ledger category mutation.
- Identical idempotent requests return the stored draft result; conflicting reuse preserves the original row.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do not implement generic upsert or update a prior rule row in place - rejected by DD-CLASSIFY-STATE-STORE.
- ❌ Do not activate a rule, grant broad authority, or mutate Ledger from rule.save.
- ❌ Do not query private Ledger storage or accept a category not proven active through the public contract.
- ❌ Do not place business validation in ClassifyContractMapper or ClassifyRowMapper.

## Approach
Implement rule.save with canonical conditions, current category validation, immutable versions, attribution, and no activation side effect.

Constraints:
- Expected failures return CommandResult values; all async calls propagate CancellationToken.

Expected outputs:
- SaveClassificationRuleCommand
- ClassificationRuleStore
- Immutable draft persistence

- Consumes: ClassificationRuleVocabulary (DM-CLASSIFY-RULE-VOCABULARY)

- Consumes: LedgerContractClient.ListClassificationCategoriesAsync (DM-CLASSIFY-LEDGER-PROJECTION-CONTRACT)

title: Define INSIGHTS analytical contracts
description:
## Objective
Every analytical INSIGHTS data shape is represented by one deterministic Native-AOT-safe contract without transport, persistence, or UI behavior.

## Implements
- FR-INSIGHTS-CONTRACT-DISCOVERY: Discover the Public INSIGHTS Operation contract
  - AC: Given a compatible caller with no financial input, when operation discovery is requested, then every Public INSIGHTS Operation is returned in canonical verb order with stable operation identity and contract version.
  - AC: Given one discovered operation, when its descriptor is inspected, then request and result schema fingerprints, mutability, authority, idempotency requirement, limits, stable error types, exit categories, and compatibility range are explicit.
  - AC: Given policy discovery, when the catalogue is returned, then every released Analysis Window, formula, Evidence Sufficiency, severity, explanation, and ordering policy has stable kind, version, status, and fingerprint metadata.
  - AC: Given a formally deferred Forecast, Trend, Anomaly, or Attention Item policy, when policy discovery is requested, then it is marked unsupported and no executable formula or threshold is advertised.
  - AC: Given INSIGHTS authority metadata, when it is inspected, then no LEDGER, CLASSIFY, or BUDGET mutation operation is present.
  - AC: Given an unsupported INSIGHTS contract version, when discovery is requested, then one stable compatibility failure is returned without reading financial data.
  - AC: Given discovery, help, or schema output, when all fields are inspected, then no report payload, amount, merchant text, private path, permission seed, role template, menu seed, translation key, or frontend key model is present.

## Depends On
- None; this bead is a planned execution root.

## In Scope
- Create the closed source-generated policy, coherent evidence, analytical state, explanation, and report records used before retained-state work begins.
- Produce: Native-AOT-safe analytical contract models
- Produce: Analytical schema and privacy tests

## Out of Scope

## Success Criteria
- The contract assembly exposes closed enums and immutable records for policy descriptors, plan states, exact money and rationals, windows, metrics, pace states, evidence states, explanations, provenance, and InsightReport.
- Canonical report contracts exclude raw merchant descriptions, canonical transaction payloads, producer cursors, private evaluation rows, and dated actual members; only BoundInsightEvidence may carry dated members as ephemeral compiler input.
- All money is signed checked Int64 ZAR minor units, rationals have a positive denominator and canonical normalization, IDs are opaque stable values, and every collection documents deterministic ordering.
- The semantic content fingerprint includes every visible metric, state, explanation, provenance item, policy version, and source identity while excluding derived reportId and contentFingerprint fields.
- Source-generated serialization rejects unknown fields and produces byte-stable schema fingerprints under repeated builds.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do NOT use string constants for system-owned states or statuses; use closed enums per ADR-CORE-0004.
- ❌ Do NOT add HTTP DTOs, frontend models, EF entities, policy scripts, arbitrary formulas, or caller-authored report payloads.
- ❌ Do NOT place raw merchant text, canonical transactions, producer cursors, or private evaluation rows in any analytical contract.
- ❌ Do NOT include reportId or contentFingerprint in the semantic payload that is hashed.

## Approach
Create the closed source-generated policy, coherent evidence, analytical state, explanation, and report records used before retained-state work begins.

title: Release the LEDGER-owned classification contract
description:
## Objective
Ledger exposes versioned evaluation and apply-preflight projections plus drift-safe assignment and correction contracts without exposing private storage.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-APPLY-EXECUTION: Apply authorized decisions through public LEDGER operations
  - AC: Given an authorized selection whose evaluation, projection, category, normalization, and rule-set fingerprints are current, when apply starts, then CLASSIFY completes preflight before the first LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given any stale or incompatible item detected during preflight, when apply starts, then CLASSIFY rejects the whole requested selection before the first LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given an authorized uncategorized active transaction and active category, when its item is submitted, then CLASSIFY invokes only the public LEDGER category-assignment operation with a stable per-transaction idempotency identity.
  - AC: Given an already categorized transaction, when a correction is explicitly selected, then CLASSIFY requires a transaction-specific owner reason and never includes that correction in exact-rule broad apply.
  - AC: Given an apply request, when processing terminates, then every requested transaction has one structured result of applied, already-applied, rejected, failed, or unresolved.
  - AC: Given the same apply identity and semantically identical request, when apply is retried, then CLASSIFY returns the prior terminal item results and creates no second category mutation.
  - AC: Given an apply identity reused with different selection, category, mode, fingerprint, or reason, when apply is retried, then CLASSIFY returns a stable conflict and preserves the original results.
  - AC: Given interruption between item submissions, when the same apply run is resumed, then completed items reconcile from durable results and processing continues only from the exact unresolved frontier.
- FR-CLASSIFY-ELIGIBLE-PROJECTION: Obtain the eligible classification projection
  - AC: Given a compatible public LEDGER contract, when the classification projection schema is discovered, then it explicitly defines the allowed rule-input fields, canonical eligibility states, stable ordering, snapshot identity, expiry behavior, and category-catalogue version.
  - AC: Given an explicit evaluation request, when CLASSIFY obtains the first projection page, then the request selects active transactions requiring an independent category decision under public categorization, transfer, refund, relationship, and lifecycle state.
  - AC: Given a transaction that public LEDGER state marks inactive, when the projection is obtained, then that transaction is not eligible for an independent CLASSIFY decision.
  - AC: Given a transaction that public LEDGER state marks already independently categorized, when the projection is obtained, then that transaction is not eligible for an independent CLASSIFY decision.
  - AC: Given a transaction that public LEDGER state marks as an active owned-transfer principal leg, when the projection is obtained, then that transaction is not eligible for an independent CLASSIFY decision.
  - AC: Given a transaction that public LEDGER state marks as a linked refund or reversal whose category follows its original, when the projection is obtained, then that transaction is not eligible for an independent CLASSIFY decision.
  - AC: Given a projection spanning multiple pages, when every page is consumed through the snapshot cursor, then membership and order remain those of the first-page snapshot and every ordinal appears exactly once.
  - AC: Given an unavailable or incompatible LEDGER operation or projection version, when evaluation is requested, then CLASSIFY returns a stable compatibility failure before creating an evaluation outcome.
  - AC: Given an expired or invalid snapshot cursor before complete projection acquisition, when evaluation continues, then CLASSIFY returns a stable stale-input failure and publishes no partial evaluation.
  - AC: Given transactions across accounts that contribute to one shared budget pool, when CLASSIFY evaluates them, then category identity remains cross-account and no per-account budget envelope or classifier rule set is inferred; account.id is inspected only when an explicit rule condition states that descriptor meaning differs.
  - AC: Given active transfer principal or linked-refund state, when eligibility is determined, then CLASSIFY consumes the Ledger-owned relationship outcome and never reconstructs transfer or refund linkage from description evidence.

## Depends On
- None; this is an initial ready-frontier bead.

## In Scope
Extend the LEDGER-owned public Actuals and category-allocation contracts with the purpose-scoped classification projection and atomic mutation preconditions required by CLASSIFY.

- Versioned classification_v1 projection contracts
- Ledger-owned mutation-state and revision preconditions
- Focused projection and stale-write tests

## Out of Scope
- bd-2q0i (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-INT-LEDGER-CONTRACT) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- Do not modify files reserved by sibling beads or implement any capability outside the twelve-operation CLASSIFY v1 surface.

## Success Criteria
- Given purpose=evaluation, the public projection returns only active transactions requiring an independent category decision and preserves complete snapshot order across pages.
- Given purpose=apply_preflight and bounded transaction IDs, every selected identity is returned or reported missing with assignable, correctable, or ineligible state plus current allocation and lifecycle revisions.
- Given an assignment with an existing allocation or a correction whose expected allocation or revision drifted, Ledger returns a stable stale-precondition result and appends no allocation.
- Given an incompatible projection or mutation contract version, descriptor validation fails before financial-data read or mutation.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do not add a private classification query or direct CLASSIFY access to Ledger storage - rejected by DD-CLASSIFY-LEDGER-PUBLIC-PROJECTION.
- ❌ Do not re-infer transfer, refund, lifecycle, categorization, or allocation eligibility outside Ledger - rejected by DD-CLASSIFY-LEDGER-PUBLIC-PROJECTION.
- ❌ Do not permit correction without the exact expected active allocation and projection revisions - the race would violate DD-CLASSIFY-LEDGER-PUBLIC-PROJECTION.
- ❌ Do not mutate transaction source facts or historical allocation rows.

## Approach
Extend the LEDGER-owned public Actuals and category-allocation contracts with the purpose-scoped classification projection and atomic mutation preconditions required by CLASSIFY.

Constraints:
- This is a LEDGER-owned public contract change even though it is a prerequisite in PLAN-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-V1; implementation and review must preserve LEDGER module authority.

design:
Read one detailed batch or a protected 15-minute metadata snapshot page and return only complete durable safe-error guidance and immutable snapshot membership.

acceptance_criteria:
With batchId, status returns BatchStatusDetail from retained INGEST state without source or Ledger access: metadata-only summary, manifest revision, approval, receipt state, terminal counts, unresolved frontier, latest complete BatchErrorEvent, retained artifact kinds, and next allowed operations.
Without batchId, limit defaults to 50 and accepts only 1 through 100; the first request uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE to materialize all retained metadata-only summaries into one 15-minute status_snapshot ordered by updatedAt descending then batchId.

The opaque cursor binds cursor version, contract version, snapshotId, next ordinal, page size, store generation, and expiry to the protected snapshot header; malformed, unknown, expired, mismatched, or out-of-range cursors fail closed.

Pre-commit failures report mutationPossibility=none and no committable manifest; commit-stage failures report possible or confirmed only from durable evidence, exact completed outcomes, unresolved frontier, and resume or abandon guidance.
Every expected batch failure returns the exact durable code, category, safeMessage, candidateId, mutationPossibility, durableState, retryAction, and field from BatchErrorEvent; no field is inferred from candidate_receipt.error_code.
StatusOperationModule binds ingest.status but global registration waits for the public-contract gate.

Confirm every status field derives from durable state and the handler performs no mutation.

## Objective
The Budget Position and INSIGHTS member contracts carry the direct/descendant partition and frozen Spend Category ancestry, and the calculation schema version advances to `budget-position-v2`.

## Implements
- FR-BUDGET-POSITION-QUERY: Calculate exact Budget Positions

title: Verify bounded correction feedback
description:
## Objective
UC-CLASSIFY-005 proves corrections remain authoritative in Ledger while CLASSIFY records only attributable bounded non-active feedback proposals.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-CORRECTION-FEEDBACK: Turn owner corrections into bounded feedback
  - AC: Given an accepted or rejected outcome, when feedback is recorded, then it references the exact transaction, evaluation, outcome, normalization, rule-set, and contributing rule versions plus owner actor, reason, and timestamp.
  - AC: Given a category correction completed in LEDGER, when CLASSIFY records feedback, then it references the authoritative prior and resulting Ledger allocations without rewriting either.
  - AC: Given one correction, when CLASSIFY derives a response, then it records no proposal or one smallest-scope retire, narrow, or replacement proposal.
  - AC: Given a feedback-derived proposal, when it is recorded, then CLASSIFY does not activate the proposal automatically.
  - AC: Given a feedback-derived proposal, when it is recorded, then CLASSIFY does not broaden an existing rule automatically.
  - AC: Given a feedback-derived candidate, when activation is requested, then the same private validation and explicit activation requirements as any other candidate apply.
  - AC: Given historical feedback, when a rule is retired or superseded, then the feedback remains attributable to the original rule version and outcome.
  - AC: Given unavailable prior Match Evidence, when feedback is recorded, then CLASSIFY stores the owner decision but creates no rule proposal from reconstructed current evidence.
  - AC: Given an accepted or rejected suggestion, when feedback is recorded, then CLASSIFY may record no proposal and never invents a rule change merely because the owner accepted or rejected one outcome.
  - AC: Given a transaction-specific correction, when feedback is recorded, then the authoritative transaction correction remains separate from every reusable rule draft and is never generalized from that row without the normal save, validation, and activation path.
- FR-CLASSIFY-STATE-RETENTION-CLEANUP: Retain attributable state and clean derived artifacts
  - AC: Given an activated rule, apply result, or feedback record, when retention is inspected, then CLASSIFY retains the minimal actor, reason, timestamp, stable references, fingerprints, prior state, and resulting state required for explanation and replay.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path succeeds, when its result is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path returns an expected failure, when its result is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path returns an unexpected handled failure, when its failure is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given an unreferenced draft rule, validation run, or evaluation run, when the owner explicitly abandons it, then it becomes non-activatable and its removable derived payload is deleted without changing active rules or LEDGER.
  - AC: Given a rule version, evaluation, or apply result referenced by active state, Ledger mutation provenance, or feedback, when hard removal is requested, then CLASSIFY rejects removal and requires lifecycle retirement or retained history.
  - AC: Given process startup, when orphan temporary artifacts from a prior crash are found, then CLASSIFY validates ownership and removes only recognized CLASSIFY temporaries before accepting new mutation.
  - AC: Given cleanup completion, when status is requested, then it returns cleanup run ID, policy version, removed artifact count, retained artifact count, and per-kind counts but no removed payload or path.
- FR-CLASSIFY-STATUS-HISTORY: Inspect classification status and history
  - AC: Given a status request, when current rule state is returned, then it identifies the active Rule Set Version and draft, active, retired, and superseded rule versions with rule version ID, Rule Set Version ID, lifecycle state, actor ID, reason code, created-at timestamp, and predecessor or successor IDs.
  - AC: Given a retained validation or evaluation run, when status is requested, then it returns its fingerprint, lifecycle state, aggregate outcome counts, staleness state, and exactly one next-operation enum value without rereading the corpus or LEDGER projection.
  - AC: Given a retained apply run, when status is requested, then it returns the authorized fingerprint, terminal item totals, unresolved frontier, and whether replay or resume is safe.
  - AC: Given retained feedback, when status is requested, then it returns the referenced outcome, decision type, proposal state, actor, reason, and rule versions without reconstructing evidence.
  - AC: Given an unknown status subject, when status is requested, then CLASSIFY returns stable not-found and does not search private payloads heuristically.
  - AC: Given any expected failure, when status is returned, then it identifies whether CLASSIFY or LEDGER mutation may have occurred and returns exactly one permitted next-operation enum value from retry, resume, re-evaluate, correct, abandon, cleanup, or none.

## Depends On
- bd-3tzh (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-FEEDBACK-PROPOSALS): The UC verifies the complete feedback and proposal slice.

title: Tally CLI hangs forever when stdin is redirected but never closed (Program.cs:64) — read stdin only when the operation needs input
description: Diagnosed 2026-07-28 while unblocking a 6h-hung Ingest verification run. Program.cs:64-66 does 'Console.IsInputRedirected ? await Console.In.ReadToEndAsync(ct) : null', so the binary drains stdin to EOF for EVERY invocation whose stdin is redirected — including operations that consume no input such as 'schema list'. Proven with the built binary: stdin </dev/null -> exit 0 with 532KB JSON; stdin an open pipe with no data -> hangs indefinitely (timeout 124, zero output). Observed live: testhost-spawned 'tally schema list' (PID 1527345) blocked in unix_stream_data_wait on fd0 for 6h09m, wedging dotnet test. PublishedTallyFixture.RunAsync does call StandardInput.Close(), so the surviving write end is most likely inherited by a concurrently-spawned sibling child of the shared testhost (matches 'passes alone, hangs in the combined suite'). FIX (product): only read stdin when the resolved operation declares it needs input (e.g. --input - present), leaving no-input operations immune. FIX (tests, defensive): give PublishedTallyFixture.RunAsync a bounded WaitForExitAsync timeout so this class of stall fails loudly instead of hanging. Related but distinct from bd-80rh (peak-RSS parallel interference).

title: Acquire bounded Ledger evaluation input
description:
## Objective
Evaluation receives one bounded, compatible, completely paged Ledger snapshot or a stable pre-state failure.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-ELIGIBLE-PROJECTION: Obtain the eligible classification projection
  - AC: Given a compatible public LEDGER contract, when the classification projection schema is discovered, then it explicitly defines the allowed rule-input fields, canonical eligibility states, stable ordering, snapshot identity, expiry behavior, and category-catalogue version.
  - AC: Given an explicit evaluation request, when CLASSIFY obtains the first projection page, then the request selects active transactions requiring an independent category decision under public categorization, transfer, refund, relationship, and lifecycle state.
  - AC: Given a transaction that public LEDGER state marks inactive, when the projection is obtained, then that transaction is not eligible for an independent CLASSIFY decision.
  - AC: Given a transaction that public LEDGER state marks already independently categorized, when the projection is obtained, then that transaction is not eligible for an independent CLASSIFY decision.
  - AC: Given a transaction that public LEDGER state marks as an active owned-transfer principal leg, when the projection is obtained, then that transaction is not eligible for an independent CLASSIFY decision.
  - AC: Given a transaction that public LEDGER state marks as a linked refund or reversal whose category follows its original, when the projection is obtained, then that transaction is not eligible for an independent CLASSIFY decision.
  - AC: Given a projection spanning multiple pages, when every page is consumed through the snapshot cursor, then membership and order remain those of the first-page snapshot and every ordinal appears exactly once.
  - AC: Given an unavailable or incompatible LEDGER operation or projection version, when evaluation is requested, then CLASSIFY returns a stable compatibility failure before creating an evaluation outcome.
  - AC: Given an expired or invalid snapshot cursor before complete projection acquisition, when evaluation continues, then CLASSIFY returns a stable stale-input failure and publishes no partial evaluation.
  - AC: Given transactions across accounts that contribute to one shared budget pool, when CLASSIFY evaluates them, then category identity remains cross-account and no per-account budget envelope or classifier rule set is inferred; account.id is inspected only when an explicit rule condition states that descriptor meaning differs.
  - AC: Given active transfer principal or linked-refund state, when eligibility is determined, then CLASSIFY consumes the Ledger-owned relationship outcome and never reconstructs transfer or refund linkage from description evidence.

## Depends On
- bd-2olb (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-LEDGER-CLASSIFICATION-CLIENT): Input acquisition uses the verified purpose=evaluation client method.

## In Scope
Validate the public Ledger descriptor and buffer one complete ordered evaluation snapshot before classification state exists.

- ClassificationEvaluationInputLoader
- Bounded immutable evaluation input

## Out of Scope
- bd-8uew (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-EVALUATION-WORKFLOW) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- Do not modify files reserved by sibling beads or implement any capability outside the twelve-operation CLASSIFY v1 surface.

## Success Criteria
- The loader validates purpose=evaluation, classification_v1, projection version, category lifecycle, store generation, snapshot expiry, and the 10000-row bound before returning input.
- All pages are buffered in ordinal order; missing or duplicate ordinals, cursor expiry, page failure, incompatible descriptors, exact-limit overflow, or cancellation returns a stable failure and no evaluation input.
- A successful result contains only the bounded public projection fields and one immutable snapshot fingerprint; it creates no CLASSIFY state and performs no Ledger mutation.
- Repeated acquisition of an unchanged snapshot returns byte-equivalent ordered input and fingerprints.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do not open Ledger storage, infer eligibility, or reimplement Ledger lifecycle and allocation rules - per DD-CLASSIFY-LEDGER-PUBLIC-PROJECTION.
- ❌ Do not stream partial pages into CLASSIFY persistence or classification evaluation.
- ❌ Do not retain raw descriptions or page payloads after the command boundary.

## Approach
Validate the public Ledger descriptor and buffer one complete ordered evaluation snapshot before classification state exists.

Constraints:
- Propagate CancellationToken across every page request and discard buffered input on any failure.

Expected outputs:
- ClassificationEvaluationInputLoader
- Bounded immutable evaluation input

- Produces: ClassificationEvaluationInputLoader.LoadAsync (DM-CLASSIFY-EVALUATION-OUTCOME)

## Failure Criteria

Create the shared versioned base64url cursor codec and filter fingerprint policy for outcome and rule pages.

title: Implement exact Linear Pace classification
description:
## Objective
LinearPaceCalculator classifies supported plan evidence exactly, handles zero plans without division, and names every unavailable condition.

## Implements
- FR-INSIGHTS-LINEAR-PACE: Calculate a transparent linear pace state
  - AC: Given a started Budget Period with a plan, when a Linear Pace Baseline is calculated, then elapsed calendar days include the As-of local date and total calendar days equal the complete Budget Period length.
  - AC: Given a non-zero planned amount, when the baseline is calculated, then it equals planned minor units multiplied by elapsed days divided by total days as an exact rational value with no floating-point arithmetic.
  - AC: Given exact recorded actual and the exact rational baseline, when pace is classified, then actual greater than the full planned amount returns Over Plan; otherwise exact comparison with the baseline returns Below Linear Baseline, At Linear Baseline, or Above Linear Baseline.
  - AC: Given a zero planned amount with positive recorded actual, when pace is classified, then Over Zero Plan is returned without division.
  - AC: Given a zero planned amount with zero or negative recorded actual, when pace is classified, then At Or Below Zero Plan is returned without division.
  - AC: Given no plan, no active or explicit revision, a not-started period, or unavailable coherent actual evidence, when pace is requested, then the exact named unavailable state is returned and no baseline is fabricated.
  - AC: Given any Linear Pace result, when its explanation is returned, then it states the elapsed-day fraction, formula version, exact inputs, current-day incompleteness possibility, and that the baseline assumes uniform calendar distribution and is not a Forecast.
  - AC: Given daily or weekly exact metrics, when pace output is inspected, then no separate daily or weekly sub-budget is invented from the monthly plan.

## Depends On
- bd-1qz (TASK-INSIGHTS-CONTRACT-MODELS): The calculator returns ExactRational and PaceResult contracts.

## In Scope
- Compute the approved month-to-date exact rational baseline and closed pace states with explicit limitations.
- Produce: LinearPaceCalculator
- Produce: Exact boundary-state tests

## Out of Scope
- No sibling handoff beyond the explicit Depends On and Failure Criteria contracts.

## Success Criteria
- For a started period with a non-zero plan, the exact baseline is plannedMinorUnits multiplied by elapsed inclusive calendar days divided by total period days with canonical exact rational arithmetic.
- Actual greater than the full plan returns OverPlan before baseline comparison; otherwise exact comparison returns BelowLinearBaseline, AtLinearBaseline, or AboveLinearBaseline.
- A zero plan with positive actual returns OverZeroPlan; zero or negative actual returns AtOrBelowZeroPlan without division.
- NoBudgetPlan, NoActiveBudgetPlanRevision, future period, or unavailable coherent evidence returns the exact named unavailable state with no baseline.
- Every result cites exact inputs, elapsed fraction, formula version, current-day incompleteness, uniform-distribution limitation, and explicitly says it is not a Forecast.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do NOT use decimal rounding or floating point — rejected per DD-INSIGHTS-TRUSTED-WINDOW-PACE-POLICY.
- ❌ Do NOT divide a zero plan, infer daily or weekly sub-budgets, accept an implicit clock, or advertise Linear Pace as a Forecast.
- ❌ Do NOT return a baseline after overflow, undefined arithmetic, plan absence, future time, or incoherent evidence.

## Approach
Compute the approved month-to-date exact rational baseline and closed pace states with explicit limitations.
- Constraint: Full-plan overage precedence is evaluated before the exact baseline comparison.
- Expected output: LinearPaceCalculator
- Expected output: Exact boundary-state tests

## Interfaces
- Produces: LinearPaceCalculator.Calculate (DM-INSIGHTS-ANALYTICAL-EVIDENCE) — one closed PaceResult

  - AC: Given date-granular actual evidence, when it is consumed, then every page belongs to one public snapshot or authoritative state binding and every ordinal is present exactly once.
  - AC: Given a complete evidence set with a Budget Position, when actual members are reconciled, then each member is assigned exactly once to Budgeted, Zero Budget, Unbudgeted, or Uncategorized and every exact bucket and total equals the cited Budget Position.

title: Create and independently verify complete INSIGHTS backups
description:
## Objective
Backup publishes one complete verified artifact and durable receipt, while standalone Verify proves any candidate without changing active state or Status.

## Implements
- FR-INSIGHTS-BACKUP-VERIFY-RESTORE: Back up, verify, and restore retained INSIGHTS state
  - AC: Given a valid owner-only backup target, when Backup succeeds, then all durable Report Snapshots, Restatement links, Deletion Events, idempotency outcomes, policy metadata, and storage-version evidence are captured in one attributable point-in-time artifact.
  - AC: Given Backup, when its contents are inspected, then ephemeral producer cursors, temporary reports, private evaluation rows, raw merchant text, and unrelated upstream state are absent.
  - AC: Given a backup artifact, when Verify succeeds, then cryptographic fingerprint, format and storage compatibility, ownership and permissions, complete counts, link integrity, content fingerprints, idempotency outcomes, and deletion-state consistency are independently checked.
  - AC: Given corruption, omission, incompatible version, unsafe ownership or permissions, or failed integrity, when Verify runs, then the exact failure is returned and no active store changes.
  - AC: Given a verified compatible backup, when Restore starts, then it builds and validates a separate candidate without modifying the active store.
  - AC: Given a complete verified candidate, when Restore activates, then the selected backup state becomes authoritative atomically and the prior store remains available until activation succeeds.
  - AC: Given cancellation, crash, insufficient space, permission failure, or migration failure before activation, when recovery completes, then the prior authoritative store is unchanged.
  - AC: Given a backup created before a later report deletion, when that backup is explicitly restored, then its exact captured report and deletion state are reinstated and identified in the restore result.

## Depends On
- bd-7kn (TASK-INSIGHTS-STATE-FOUNDATION): Backup reads and verifies the complete store schema and owner-only layout.
- bd-2nv (TASK-INSIGHTS-IDEMPOTENCY-EXECUTOR): Backup uses the module replay identity and crash reservation state.

## In Scope
- Implement the replay-safe point-in-time Backup saga and read-only independent Verify operation over owner-only recognized artifacts.
- Produce: InsightsBackupService
- Produce: InsightsBackupVerifier
- Produce: CreateInsightsBackupCommand
- Produce: VerifyInsightsBackupQuery
- Produce: Backup and verification tests

## Out of Scope
- No sibling handoff beyond the explicit Depends On and Failure Criteria contracts.

## Success Criteria
- Backup requires an owner-only recognized target, actor, safe normalized path identity, and idempotency; it records one Attempting reservation with request fingerprint and deterministic artifact identity before external artifact work.
- A read-consistent candidate captures every snapshot, payload, Restatement link, DeletionEvent, prior terminal idempotency outcome, retained policy fingerprint, storage version, and count while excluding only the current non-terminal Backup reservation and all forbidden ephemeral/private data.
- InsightsBackupVerifier independently checks storage/version compatibility, owner and permissions, integrity, counts, links, payload/content/table/artifact fingerprints, terminal idempotency outcomes, deletion consistency, and policy metadata before atomic publication.
- After publication Backup records one terminal receipt; an exact retry after a crash reconciles the already published verified deterministic artifact without duplication, and a completed failure removes its reservation.
- VerifyInsightsBackupQuery is read-only: valid and invalid artifacts return exact evidence or failure, change neither active state nor Status, and expose no private path or report payload.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do NOT use an unverified SQLite file copy, include the current Attempting reservation as a terminal outcome, publish before verification, or issue a second artifact on exact crash replay.
- ❌ Do NOT persist standalone Verify results, alter CURRENT, modify the source artifact, or expose private paths and payloads — per DD-INSIGHTS-VERIFIED-RECOVERY-ACTIVATION.
- ❌ Do NOT accept unsafe ownership, permissive modes, omission, corruption, incompatible versions, dangling links, count mismatch, or fingerprint mismatch.

## Approach
Implement the replay-safe point-in-time Backup saga and read-only independent Verify operation over owner-only recognized artifacts.
