title: Execute the replay-safe apply saga
description:
## Objective
Explicit authorized assignments and corrections reach Ledger at most once per item and every crash window resolves to an exact durable frontier.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-APPLY-EXECUTION: Apply authorized decisions through public LEDGER operations
  - AC: Given an authorized selection whose evaluation, projection, category, normalization, and rule-set fingerprints are current, when apply starts, then CLASSIFY completes preflight before the first LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given any stale or incompatible item detected during preflight, when apply starts, then CLASSIFY rejects the whole requested selection before the first LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given an authorized uncategorized active transaction and active category, when its item is submitted, then CLASSIFY invokes only the public LEDGER category-assignment operation with a stable per-transaction idempotency identity.
  - AC: Given an already categorized transaction, when a correction is explicitly selected, then CLASSIFY requires a transaction-specific owner reason and never includes that correction in exact-rule broad apply.
  - AC: Given an apply request, when processing terminates, then every requested transaction has one structured result of applied, already-applied, rejected, failed, or unresolved.
  - AC: Given the same apply identity and semantically identical request, when apply is retried, then CLASSIFY returns the prior terminal item results and creates no second category mutation.
  - AC: Given an apply identity reused with different selection, category, mode, fingerprint, or reason, when apply is retried, then CLASSIFY returns a stable conflict and preserves the original results.
  - AC: Given interruption between item submissions, when the same apply run is resumed, then completed items reconcile from durable results and processing continues only from the exact unresolved frontier.

## Depends On

- bd-2olb (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-LEDGER-CLASSIFICATION-CLIENT): Apply consumes the public assignment and correction methods with frozen preconditions.

design:

title: Validate CLASSIFY local data security
description:
## Objective
Every CLASSIFY workflow remains owner-only, offline, non-interactive, payload-safe, path-safe, and free of background or remote processing.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-STATE-RETENTION-CLEANUP: Retain attributable state and clean derived artifacts
  - AC: Given an activated rule, apply result, or feedback record, when retention is inspected, then CLASSIFY retains the minimal actor, reason, timestamp, stable references, fingerprints, prior state, and resulting state required for explanation and replay.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path succeeds, when its result is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path returns an expected failure, when its result is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path returns an unexpected handled failure, when its failure is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given an unreferenced draft rule, validation run, or evaluation run, when the owner explicitly abandons it, then it becomes non-activatable and its removable derived payload is deleted without changing active rules or LEDGER.
  - AC: Given a rule version, evaluation, or apply result referenced by active state, Ledger mutation provenance, or feedback, when hard removal is requested, then CLASSIFY rejects removal and requires lifecycle retirement or retained history.
  - AC: Given process startup, when orphan temporary artifacts from a prior crash are found, then CLASSIFY validates ownership and removes only recognized CLASSIFY temporaries before accepting new mutation.
  - AC: Given cleanup completion, when status is requested, then it returns cleanup run ID, policy version, removed artifact count, retained artifact count, and per-kind counts but no removed payload or path.

## Depends On
- bd-3hcn (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-ABANDON-CLEANUP): Consumes an interface produced by TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-ABANDON-CLEANUP.
- bd-2ffc (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-APPLY-RUN-SAGA): Consumes an interface produced by TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-APPLY-RUN-SAGA.
- bd-3g6y (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-INT-PUBLIC-CONTRACT): Security validation executes every published operation through the complete process contract.
- bd-56yx (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-OWNER-RULEBOOK): Security validation includes the private owner-evidence path and report.
- bd-2fdz (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-PRIVATE-CORPUS-READER): Consumes an interface produced by TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-PRIVATE-CORPUS-READER.

## In Scope
Validation-only security gate with no implements refs; it consolidates owner identity, permissions, payload isolation, cleanup, offline operation, and hostile-input evidence.

- ClassifySecurityGateEvidence
- Security verification report

## Out of Scope
- bd-1yaj (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-GRAPH-QUALITY) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- Do not modify files reserved by sibling beads or implement any capability outside the twelve-operation CLASSIFY v1 surface.

## Success Criteria
- Success, expected failure, handled unexpected failure, interruption, resume, abandon, cleanup, and startup recovery preserve 0700 directories, 0600 files, owner identity, and zero raw corpus copies or orphan temporaries.
- Canaries in descriptions, tokens, rules, corpus rows, amounts, requests, and failures appear in none of arguments, tracked files, stdout errors, stderr, logs, telemetry, crash output, reports, or unrelated results.
- Malformed JSON, unknown fields, symlinks, permissive modes, wrong owners, unknown files, outside-root paths, over-limits, and incompatible versions fail before activation or Ledger mutation.
- Every acceptance workflow completes with network denied, no prompt or TTY read, and no Tally daemon, watcher, scheduler, child process, or background worker before or after invocation.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do not redact only logs while leaving payloads in arguments, errors, crash files, telemetry, tracked artifacts, or temporary storage.
- ❌ Do not skip permission, symlink, path traversal, crash, or network-denied cases on linux-x64.
- ❌ Do not use cloud inference, remote embeddings, third-party processing, a daemon, or a hidden child process.
- ❌ Do not mark this validation-only gate green from unit tests alone; execute the published Native-AOT binary.

## Approach
Validation-only security gate with no implements refs; it consolidates owner identity, permissions, payload isolation, cleanup, offline operation, and hostile-input evidence.

title: Validate candidate rule sets privately
description:
## Objective
Candidate rules receive aggregate private evidence that blocks unsafe activation without retaining private rows.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-RULE-VALIDATION: Validate candidate rule sets against private evidence
  - AC: Given a candidate normalization or Rule Set Version and an owner-only corpus, when validation starts, then the run records the candidate, corpus, expected-outcome, category-catalogue, projection-contract, and normalization fingerprints.
  - AC: Given a completed validation run, when its report is returned, then every corpus row is accounted for and aggregate totals report suggestions, no-suggestions, conflicts, stale rows, drift canaries, and incorrect-application canaries.
  - AC: Given any missing or stale required fingerprint, when activation is attempted, then CLASSIFY rejects activation without changing the active Rule Set Version.
  - AC: Given any incorrect-application canary, when activation is attempted, then CLASSIFY rejects activation without changing the active Rule Set Version.
  - AC: Given any unexplained incompatible-category conflict in required evidence, when activation is attempted, then CLASSIFY rejects activation without changing the active Rule Set Version.
  - AC: Given an unavailable private corpus, when an existing active rule set is evaluated, then CLASSIFY may use that unchanged active version.
  - AC: Given an unavailable private corpus, when a new rule or normalization version is activated, then CLASSIFY rejects activation without changing the active Rule Set Version.
  - AC: Given an unavailable private corpus, when broad-apply authorization is requested, then CLASSIFY rejects authorization before LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given a validation report, when it is persisted or exported, then it contains corpus fingerprints and aggregate outcomes but no raw transaction description, normalized token, financial value, or expected-outcome row.
  - AC: Given an owner-authored candidate rulebook, when its pre-authority gate runs, then every private row is accounted for exactly once, incorrect applications and unexplained incompatible conflicts are zero, coverage and no-suggestion totals are explicit, drift canaries and deterministic fingerprints are stable, and owner decision and time benefit are measured.
  - AC: Given owner-authored safety passes but measured benefit is insufficient for broad authority, when activation or exact-rule broad apply is considered, then CLASSIFY requires an explicit product decision and does not invent a 50 percent benefit threshold.

## Depends On
- bd-2sde (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-DETERMINISTIC-ENGINE): Consumes an interface produced by TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-DETERMINISTIC-ENGINE.
- bd-2olb (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-LEDGER-CLASSIFICATION-CLIENT): Validation binds the current public projection and category lifecycle contract.

## In Scope

- Aggregate ValidationReport

title: Implement module-wide retained-operation replay
description:
## Objective
InsightsIdempotencyExecutor returns prior logical outcomes for exact retries, rejects changed input, and never consumes failed request identities or leaks deleted content.

## Implements
- None; this task is a validation or shared-contract task with no direct FR ownership.

## Depends On
- bd-7kn (TASK-INSIGHTS-STATE-FOUNDATION): The replay executor uses the idempotency table and caller-owned SQLite transactions.

## In Scope
- Create the transactional Attempting and Succeeded replay coordinator consumed by Retain, Restate, Delete, Backup, and Restore.
- Produce: InsightsIdempotencyExecutor
- Produce: Replay conflict and crash-state tests

## Out of Scope
- Recovery handlers use the same identity model but own their external artifact saga.

## Success Criteria
- The unique replay identity is operationId plus contractVersion plus keyDigest; the canonical request fingerprint includes every logical input, actor, reason, target or predecessor, selected policies, and expected-current fingerprint; Backup and Restore additionally include safe normalized path identity.
- A Succeeded record with the same key and fingerprint returns the exact prior logical outcome before TimeProvider, producer, or write access; the same key with a changed fingerprint returns IdempotencyConflict and changes nothing.
- New write attempts are reserved transactionally; success stores one immutable outcome reference; validation, cancellation, transient, generation, and persistence failure leave no successful outcome and remove any completed-failure reservation.
- If a retained snapshot outcome was later deleted, replay resolves to metadata-only Deleted evidence and never recreates or discloses the removed payload.
- Backup-specific Attempting reconciliation can retain deterministic artifact identity across a crash while the copied artifact excludes the current non-terminal reservation.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do NOT store full requests, reports, private paths, or caller idempotency keys; persist digests, fingerprints, safe identities, and outcome refs only.
- ❌ Do NOT treat expected failures as exceptions, consume a failed request identity, create a second logical outcome, or replay deleted content.
- ❌ Do NOT implement a generic event-sourcing system — rejected per DD-INSIGHTS-RETENTION-RESTATEMENT-LIFECYCLE.

## Approach
Create the transactional Attempting and Succeeded replay coordinator consumed by Retain, Restate, Delete, Backup, and Restore.
- Constraint: The executor participates in the caller-owned SQLite transaction and has one production implementation.
- Expected output: InsightsIdempotencyExecutor
- Expected output: Replay conflict and crash-state tests

## Interfaces
- Consumes: InsightsStateStore (DM-INSIGHTS-STATE-STORE) — transaction and replay rows
- Produces: InsightsIdempotencyExecutor.ExecuteAsync (DM-INSIGHTS-IDEMPOTENCY) — new, replay, conflict, or failed reservation result

title: Extend the shared Ledger contract client
description:
## Objective
CLASSIFY consumes only released Ledger operations through one concrete replay-safe LedgerContractClient.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-APPLY-EXECUTION: Apply authorized decisions through public LEDGER operations
  - AC: Given an authorized selection whose evaluation, projection, category, normalization, and rule-set fingerprints are current, when apply starts, then CLASSIFY completes preflight before the first LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given any stale or incompatible item detected during preflight, when apply starts, then CLASSIFY rejects the whole requested selection before the first LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given an authorized uncategorized active transaction and active category, when its item is submitted, then CLASSIFY invokes only the public LEDGER category-assignment operation with a stable per-transaction idempotency identity.
  - AC: Given an already categorized transaction, when a correction is explicitly selected, then CLASSIFY requires a transaction-specific owner reason and never includes that correction in exact-rule broad apply.
  - AC: Given an apply request, when processing terminates, then every requested transaction has one structured result of applied, already-applied, rejected, failed, or unresolved.
  - AC: Given the same apply identity and semantically identical request, when apply is retried, then CLASSIFY returns the prior terminal item results and creates no second category mutation.
  - AC: Given an apply identity reused with different selection, category, mode, fingerprint, or reason, when apply is retried, then CLASSIFY returns a stable conflict and preserves the original results.
  - AC: Given interruption between item submissions, when the same apply run is resumed, then completed items reconcile from durable results and processing continues only from the exact unresolved frontier.
- FR-CLASSIFY-ELIGIBLE-PROJECTION: Obtain the eligible classification projection
  - AC: Given a compatible public LEDGER contract, when the classification projection schema is discovered, then it explicitly defines the allowed rule-input fields, canonical eligibility states, stable ordering, snapshot identity, expiry behavior, and category-catalogue version.
  - AC: Given an explicit evaluation request, when CLASSIFY obtains the first projection page, then the request selects active transactions requiring an independent category decision under public categorization, transfer, refund, relationship, and lifecycle state.
  - AC: Given a transaction that public LEDGER state marks inactive, when the projection is obtained, then that transaction is not eligible for an independent CLASSIFY decision.
  - AC: Given a transaction that public LEDGER state marks already independently categorized, when the projection is obtained, then that transaction is not eligible for an independent CLASSIFY decision.
  - AC: Given a transaction that public LEDGER state marks as an active owned-transfer principal leg, when the projection is obtained, then that transaction is not eligible for an independent CLASSIFY decision.
  - AC: Given a transaction that public LEDGER state marks as a linked refund or reversal whose category follows its original, when the projection is obtained, then that transaction is not eligible for an independent CLASSIFY decision.
  - AC: Given a projection spanning multiple pages, when every page is consumed through the snapshot cursor, then membership and order remain those of the first-page snapshot and every ordinal appears exactly once.
  - AC: Given an unavailable or incompatible LEDGER operation or projection version, when evaluation is requested, then CLASSIFY returns a stable compatibility failure before creating an evaluation outcome.
  - AC: Given an expired or invalid snapshot cursor before complete projection acquisition, when evaluation continues, then CLASSIFY returns a stable stale-input failure and publishes no partial evaluation.
  - AC: Given transactions across accounts that contribute to one shared budget pool, when CLASSIFY evaluates them, then category identity remains cross-account and no per-account budget envelope or classifier rule set is inferred; account.id is inspected only when an explicit rule condition states that descriptor meaning differs.
  - AC: Given active transfer principal or linked-refund state, when eligibility is determined, then CLASSIFY consumes the Ledger-owned relationship outcome and never reconstructs transfer or refund linkage from description evidence.

## Depends On
- bd-2q0i (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-INT-LEDGER-CONTRACT): The client may consume only the prerequisite contract proven by this gate.

## In Scope
Add CLASSIFY projection, category-display, assignment, and correction methods to the concrete client created by INGEST.

- Classification methods on the shared LedgerContractClient
- Public-boundary and error-preservation tests

## Out of Scope
- bd-gv0z (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-APPLY-PREVIEW) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- bd-2ffc (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-APPLY-RUN-SAGA) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- bd-25a7 (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-EVALUATION-INPUT) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- Do not modify files reserved by sibling beads or implement any capability outside the twelve-operation CLASSIFY v1 surface.

## Success Criteria
- QueryClassificationProjectionAsync discovers a compatible descriptor before reading and consumes every page with exact ordinal accounting.
- AssignCategoryAsync and CorrectCategoryAsync preserve the frozen idempotency key, expected allocation, revisions, cancellation, and Ledger result without semantic translation.
- Unsupported versions and downstream expected failures return stable CLASSIFY-consumable result values before any private read or mutation.
- Source-reference guards prove the client uses only contracts and the shared public executor.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do not spawn the tally CLI as a child process - rejected by DD-CLASSIFY-LEDGER-PUBLIC-PROJECTION.
- ❌ Do not add a second Ledger client interface or speculative ports - rejected by DD-CLASSIFY-APPLICATION-ARCHITECTURE.
- ❌ Do not reference LedgerDb, SQLite, private handlers, or private domain types.
- ❌ Do not drop CancellationToken or rewrite Ledger error categories.

## Approach
Add CLASSIFY projection, category-display, assignment, and correction methods to the concrete client created by INGEST.

Constraints:
- Modify the client produced by TASK-INGEST-LEDGER-PUBLIC-CLIENT; keep its INGEST methods intact.

Expected outputs:
- Classification methods on the shared LedgerContractClient
- Public-boundary and error-preservation tests

## Interfaces
- Consumes: VerifiedLedgerClassificationContract (DM-CLASSIFY-LEDGER-PROJECTION-CONTRACT)
- Produces: LedgerContractClient.QueryClassificationProjectionAsync (DM-CLASSIFY-LEDGER-PROJECTION-CONTRACT)
- Produces: LedgerContractClient.ListClassificationCategoriesAsync (DM-CLASSIFY-LEDGER-PROJECTION-CONTRACT)
- Produces: LedgerContractClient.AssignCategoryAsync (DM-CLASSIFY-LEDGER-PROJECTION-CONTRACT)
- Produces: LedgerContractClient.CorrectCategoryAsync (DM-CLASSIFY-LEDGER-PROJECTION-CONTRACT)

- **Test:** `dotnet test tests/Tally.Tests/Tally.Tests.csproj --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~ClassifyLedgerContractClientTests|FullyQualifiedName~ClassifyLedgerBoundaryArchitectureTests'` — exit 0; at least 16 paging, version, assignment, correction, replay, cancellation, error-preservation, and source-boundary cases are discovered and 0 fail

title: Verify rule management and validation
description:
## Objective
UC-CLASSIFY-004 proves immutable owner-approved rule lifecycle with fail-closed private evidence and no transaction assignment.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-RULE-LIFECYCLE: Manage versioned deterministic rules
  - AC: Given a supported predicate over schema-allowed fields and an active category identifier, when a rule draft is saved, then CLASSIFY records a new immutable draft version with owner, reason, scope, normalization version, and proposed category.
  - AC: Given a rule draft is saved, when the operation completes, then no rule or Rule Set Version is activated and no LEDGER mutation occurs.
  - AC: Given an unsupported field or predicate, when a rule draft is saved, then CLASSIFY returns stable field-level validation errors and creates no activatable version.
  - AC: Given a category identifier is missing from the current catalogue, when a rule draft is saved, then CLASSIFY returns a stable category-not-found error and creates no activatable version.
  - AC: Given a category identifier is archived in the current catalogue, when a rule draft is saved, then CLASSIFY returns a stable category-inactive error and creates no activatable version.
  - AC: Given a draft whose required private validation passed, when the owner explicitly activates it, then CLASSIFY creates a new immutable active Rule Set Version containing the exact activated rule version.
  - AC: Given an active rule, when the owner retires it with a reason, then CLASSIFY creates a new active Rule Set Version without that rule and retains the retired version for inspection.
  - AC: Given an active rule that must be narrowed or replaced, when the owner activates a validated successor, then the successor references the prior version and the prior version becomes retired or superseded without in-place mutation.
  - AC: Given a category rename that preserves the same active category identifier, when rules are inspected, then their category identity is unchanged and their display name resolves to the current catalogue name.
  - AC: Given any owner decision, correction, or feedback event, when the event is recorded, then no rule version or Rule Set Version is activated automatically.
  - AC: Given a draft entered through classify.rule.save, when it is retained, then its immutable rule version records rule_origin=owner_authored and no personal rule value is compiled, seeded, logged, or exported.
  - AC: Given a draft originating from correction feedback, when it is retained, then its immutable rule version records rule_origin=feedback_derived and receives no validation, activation, broad-apply, or mutation authority from that origin.
- FR-CLASSIFY-RULE-VALIDATION: Validate candidate rule sets against private evidence
  - AC: Given a candidate normalization or Rule Set Version and an owner-only corpus, when validation starts, then the run records the candidate, corpus, expected-outcome, category-catalogue, projection-contract, and normalization fingerprints.
  - AC: Given a completed validation run, when its report is returned, then every corpus row is accounted for and aggregate totals report suggestions, no-suggestions, conflicts, stale rows, drift canaries, and incorrect-application canaries.
  - AC: Given any missing or stale required fingerprint, when activation is attempted, then CLASSIFY rejects activation without changing the active Rule Set Version.
  - AC: Given any incorrect-application canary, when activation is attempted, then CLASSIFY rejects activation without changing the active Rule Set Version.
  - AC: Given any unexplained incompatible-category conflict in required evidence, when activation is attempted, then CLASSIFY rejects activation without changing the active Rule Set Version.
  - AC: Given an unavailable private corpus, when an existing active rule set is evaluated, then CLASSIFY may use that unchanged active version.
  - AC: Given an unavailable private corpus, when a new rule or normalization version is activated, then CLASSIFY rejects activation without changing the active Rule Set Version.
  - AC: Given an unavailable private corpus, when broad-apply authorization is requested, then CLASSIFY rejects authorization before LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given a validation report, when it is persisted or exported, then it contains corpus fingerprints and aggregate outcomes but no raw transaction description, normalized token, financial value, or expected-outcome row.
  - AC: Given an owner-authored candidate rulebook, when its pre-authority gate runs, then every private row is accounted for exactly once, incorrect applications and unexplained incompatible conflicts are zero, coverage and no-suggestion totals are explicit, drift canaries and deterministic fingerprints are stable, and owner decision and time benefit are measured.
  - AC: Given owner-authored safety passes but measured benefit is insufficient for broad authority, when activation or exact-rule broad apply is considered, then CLASSIFY requires an explicit product decision and does not invent a 50 percent benefit threshold.
- FR-CLASSIFY-STATE-RETENTION-CLEANUP: Retain attributable state and clean derived artifacts
  - AC: Given an activated rule, apply result, or feedback record, when retention is inspected, then CLASSIFY retains the minimal actor, reason, timestamp, stable references, fingerprints, prior state, and resulting state required for explanation and replay.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path succeeds, when its result is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path returns an expected failure, when its result is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path returns an unexpected handled failure, when its failure is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given an unreferenced draft rule, validation run, or evaluation run, when the owner explicitly abandons it, then it becomes non-activatable and its removable derived payload is deleted without changing active rules or LEDGER.
  - AC: Given a rule version, evaluation, or apply result referenced by active state, Ledger mutation provenance, or feedback, when hard removal is requested, then CLASSIFY rejects removal and requires lifecycle retirement or retained history.
  - AC: Given process startup, when orphan temporary artifacts from a prior crash are found, then CLASSIFY validates ownership and removes only recognized CLASSIFY temporaries before accepting new mutation.
  - AC: Given cleanup completion, when status is requested, then it returns cleanup run ID, policy version, removed artifact count, retained artifact count, and per-kind counts but no removed payload or path.
- FR-CLASSIFY-STATUS-HISTORY: Inspect classification status and history
  - AC: Given a status request, when current rule state is returned, then it identifies the active Rule Set Version and draft, active, retired, and superseded rule versions with rule version ID, Rule Set Version ID, lifecycle state, actor ID, reason code, created-at timestamp, and predecessor or successor IDs.
  - AC: Given a retained validation or evaluation run, when status is requested, then it returns its fingerprint, lifecycle state, aggregate outcome counts, staleness state, and exactly one next-operation enum value without rereading the corpus or LEDGER projection.
  - AC: Given a retained apply run, when status is requested, then it returns the authorized fingerprint, terminal item totals, unresolved frontier, and whether replay or resume is safe.
  - AC: Given retained feedback, when status is requested, then it returns the referenced outcome, decision type, proposal state, actor, reason, and rule versions without reconstructing evidence.
  - AC: Given an unknown status subject, when status is requested, then CLASSIFY returns stable not-found and does not search private payloads heuristically.
  - AC: Given any expected failure, when status is returned, then it identifies whether CLASSIFY or LEDGER mutation may have occurred and returns exactly one permitted next-operation enum value from retry, resume, re-evaluate, correct, abandon, cleanup, or none.

## Depends On
- bd-3hcn (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-ABANDON-CLEANUP): UC-004 verifies safe rule-management abandonment through the public operation.
- bd-3g6y (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-INT-PUBLIC-CONTRACT): UC-004 invokes rule lifecycle operations through the published process boundary.

- AppendStatementSupersessionAsync is internal and may run only inside an authorized reconciliation writer transaction; it creates the typed statement-derived replacement and supersession while leaving all carry-forward and relationship decisions to the coordinator.
- Any replacement validation, relationship retirement, Reconciliation Exception, or write failure leaves the original state unchanged; history returns complete original/replacement facts and retained associations.
- Identical correction replay returns the original outcome; an incompatible later correction returns stable lifecycle/conflict.

title: Implement relationship revoke and replace
description:
## Objective
Retire or replace one active financial relationship atomically only after typed policies prove the resulting roles and spend effect valid.

## Implements
- FR-LEDGER-RELATIONSHIP-CORRECTION
- DD-LEDGER-FULL-AMOUNT-REFUND-RELATIONSHIP
- DD-LEDGER-IMMUTABLE-HISTORY

## Depends On

- bd-2ne: closed; provides LedgerMutationExecutor
- bd-xq6: closed; provides TransferPolicy and RelationshipStore

## In Scope
- Public relationship revoke and replace.
- Internal statement-correction replacement.
- Append-only attributable lifecycle history.
- Revalidate transfer invariants or exact same-account ZAR full-refund equality before retiring the current relationship.
- Preserve one active relationship per participant.

## Out of Scope
- Partial or cumulative refunds.
- In-place relationship edits or retirement before replacement validation.
- Bypassing TransferPolicy or RefundPolicy.
- Exposing statement replacement as an independent public command.

design: Implement append-only relationship revoke/replace using the existing lifecycle table and transaction boundary. Replacement validates the complete proposed transfer or refund before retiring the active relationship. Refund replacement reuses RefundPolicy and therefore requires same-account active ZAR transactions, correct signs, and exact absolute full-amount equality; partial, cumulative, or over-refund replacements are rejected.
acceptance_criteria:
- Public revoke appends an attributable lifecycle event, retires one active transfer or refund atomically, and removes its spend effect.
- Public replace validates the complete proposal before retirement and leaves the old relationship active on any failure.
- Replacement revalidates lifecycle, roles, cardinality, exact amount, account, currency, signs, full-refund equality, and participant exclusivity.
- Statement correction replaces only the authorized transaction and preserves every invariant, including exact full-refund equality, or returns review-required before any write.
- History retains participants, type, reason, actor/time, reconciliation decision, and replacement reference; identical replay returns the original outcome.
- No path supports partial or cumulative refunds.
notes: Corrected on 2026-07-22 after Dirk established the full-refund-only product rule. This bead consumes DD-LEDGER-FULL-AMOUNT-REFUND-RELATIONSHIP and RefundPolicy from bd-10w; cumulative-refund semantics are superseded. Pre-flight added the four established CLI integration files to the task and bead boundary so the promised typed public operations can be composed and exposed without scope drift. ASSUMPTION: Public lifecycle mutation results return the retired relationship, lifecycle event ID, and optional active replacement, following the repository's existing lifecycle-result convention.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: typed transfer/refund revoke and replace, decision-authorized statement replacement, append-only history, full-refund-only validation, and stable replay. Gates: 21 focused, 71 relationship, 568 full, build/format/AOT green.

title: Build the deterministic classification engine
description:
## Objective
One complete projection and immutable rule set produce reproducible ordered outcomes with no hidden winner or external effect.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-DETERMINISTIC-EVALUATION: Evaluate deterministic classification outcomes
  - AC: Given a complete eligible projection, active category catalogue, normalization version, and Rule Set Version, when evaluation completes, then every input ordinal has exactly one outcome of suggestion, no-suggestion, conflict, or stale and the outcome totals equal the input count.
  - AC: Given an identical Evaluation Fingerprint, when evaluation is repeated, then ordered outcomes and Match Evidence are semantically identical.
  - AC: Given exactly one matching active rule or multiple matching active rules that all propose the same active category, when a transaction is evaluated, then one suggestion names that category and every contributing rule version.
  - AC: Given active matching rules that propose different categories, when a transaction is evaluated, then the outcome is Rule Conflict with no selected category.
  - AC: Given no active matching rule, when a transaction is evaluated, then the outcome is explicit no-suggestion with no selected category.
  - AC: Given any completed evaluation, when LEDGER category history and transaction source facts are inspected, then evaluation has changed neither.
- FR-CLASSIFY-OUTCOME-INVALIDATION: Invalidate Stale Classification Outcomes
  - AC: Given a transaction becomes void in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a transaction is superseded in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a transaction allocation changes in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a transaction's transfer relationship changes in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a transaction's refund or reversal relationship changes in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a targeted category is archived, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a targeted category is reactivated, when a prior outcome created before reactivation is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a targeted category identity changes, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a category rename that preserves the same active identifier, when a prior outcome is inspected, then its category identity remains valid and the current display name is returned.
  - AC: Given the required LEDGER contract or classification projection version changes, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY identifies that changed fingerprint dimension and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given the LEDGER store generation changes, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY identifies that changed fingerprint dimension and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given the source LEDGER snapshot is invalid or expired, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY identifies that changed fingerprint dimension and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given the normalization version changes, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY identifies that changed fingerprint dimension and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given the active Rule Set Version changes, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY identifies that changed fingerprint dimension and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a stale outcome, when the owner requests the permitted next operation, then CLASSIFY returns re-evaluate and does not return correction or apply.

## Depends On
- bd-3gmq (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-RULE-VOCABULARY): The engine consumes the exact vocabulary, normalizer, and condition types.

## In Scope
Implement pure ordered matching, compatible aggregation, conflicts, fingerprints, canonical hashing, and bounded evidence.

- ClassificationEngine
- EvaluationFingerprint
- CanonicalClassificationHasher
- Bounded MatchEvidence

## Out of Scope
- bd-8uew (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-EVALUATION-WORKFLOW) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- bd-56yx (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-OWNER-RULEBOOK) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- bd-2fdz (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-PRIVATE-CORPUS-READER) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- Do not modify files reserved by sibling beads or implement any capability outside the twelve-operation CLASSIFY v1 surface.

## Success Criteria
- Every input ordinal yields exactly one suggestion, no_suggestion, conflict, or stale result and aggregate totals equal input count.
- One match or multiple same-category matches produce one suggestion naming every contributing rule version; incompatible categories produce conflict with no selected category.
- Identical fingerprints produce semantically identical ordered outcomes and evidence under repeated and permuted property cases.
- EvaluationFingerprint covers contract, projection, store generation, snapshot and expiry, category lifecycle, normalization, rule-set, and ordered item revisions.
- MatchEvidence retains only rule, condition, field, predicate, and normalized-value hash references.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do not select a winner by rule priority or input order - rejected by DD-CLASSIFY-DETERMINISTIC-EVALUATION.
- ❌ Do not publish partial streamed outcomes or perform storage or Ledger mutation from the engine.
- ❌ Do not retain full projection payloads or omit all historical evidence - both alternatives were rejected by DD-CLASSIFY-DETERMINISTIC-EVALUATION.
- ❌ Do not introduce random, clock, culture, network, or host-session inputs into matching.

## Approach
Implement pure ordered matching, compatible aggregation, conflicts, fingerprints, canonical hashing, and bounded evidence.

Constraints:
- Pure synchronous domain evaluation; all ordering and limits are explicit inputs.

Expected outputs:
- ClassificationEngine
- EvaluationFingerprint
- CanonicalClassificationHasher
- Bounded MatchEvidence

## Interfaces
- Consumes: ClassificationRuleVocabulary (DM-CLASSIFY-RULE-VOCABULARY)
- Consumes: NormalizerV1.Normalize (DM-CLASSIFY-RULE-VOCABULARY)
- Produces: ClassificationEngine.Evaluate (DM-CLASSIFY-EVALUATION-OUTCOME)
- Produces: EvaluationFingerprint.Create (DM-CLASSIFY-EVALUATION-OUTCOME)

## Files (reservation globs)
- `src/Tally/Domain/Classify/Evaluation/ClassificationEngine.cs` (create) - pure evaluator - required
- `src/Tally/Domain/Classify/Evaluation/ClassificationOutcome.cs` (create) - closed outcomes - required
- `src/Tally/Domain/Classify/Evaluation/EvaluationFingerprint.cs` (create) - staleness dimensions - required

- `tests/Tally.Tests/Classify/Evaluation/ClassificationDeterminismPropertyTests.cs` (test) - property and accounting tests - required

## Verification
- **Build:** `dotnet build Tally.slnx -c Release` — exit 0 with zero warnings and zero errors.
- **Test:** `dotnet test tests/Tally.Tests/Tally.Tests.csproj --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~ClassificationEngineTests|FullyQualifiedName~ClassificationDeterminismPropertyTests'` — exit 0; at least 40 suggestion, no-match, compatible-overlap, conflict, order, fingerprint, accounting, and permutation cases are discovered and 0 fail

title: Verify eligible deterministic evaluation
description:
## Objective
UC-CLASSIFY-001 proves complete eligible projection acquisition, deterministic outcomes, bounded failures, staleness, and zero Ledger mutation.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-DETERMINISTIC-EVALUATION: Evaluate deterministic classification outcomes
  - AC: Given a complete eligible projection, active category catalogue, normalization version, and Rule Set Version, when evaluation completes, then every input ordinal has exactly one outcome of suggestion, no-suggestion, conflict, or stale and the outcome totals equal the input count.
  - AC: Given an identical Evaluation Fingerprint, when evaluation is repeated, then ordered outcomes and Match Evidence are semantically identical.
  - AC: Given exactly one matching active rule or multiple matching active rules that all propose the same active category, when a transaction is evaluated, then one suggestion names that category and every contributing rule version.
  - AC: Given active matching rules that propose different categories, when a transaction is evaluated, then the outcome is Rule Conflict with no selected category.
  - AC: Given no active matching rule, when a transaction is evaluated, then the outcome is explicit no-suggestion with no selected category.
  - AC: Given any completed evaluation, when LEDGER category history and transaction source facts are inspected, then evaluation has changed neither.
- FR-CLASSIFY-ELIGIBLE-PROJECTION: Obtain the eligible classification projection
  - AC: Given a compatible public LEDGER contract, when the classification projection schema is discovered, then it explicitly defines the allowed rule-input fields, canonical eligibility states, stable ordering, snapshot identity, expiry behavior, and category-catalogue version.
  - AC: Given an explicit evaluation request, when CLASSIFY obtains the first projection page, then the request selects active transactions requiring an independent category decision under public categorization, transfer, refund, relationship, and lifecycle state.
  - AC: Given a transaction that public LEDGER state marks inactive, when the projection is obtained, then that transaction is not eligible for an independent CLASSIFY decision.
  - AC: Given a transaction that public LEDGER state marks already independently categorized, when the projection is obtained, then that transaction is not eligible for an independent CLASSIFY decision.
  - AC: Given a transaction that public LEDGER state marks as an active owned-transfer principal leg, when the projection is obtained, then that transaction is not eligible for an independent CLASSIFY decision.
  - AC: Given a transaction that public LEDGER state marks as a linked refund or reversal whose category follows its original, when the projection is obtained, then that transaction is not eligible for an independent CLASSIFY decision.
  - AC: Given a projection spanning multiple pages, when every page is consumed through the snapshot cursor, then membership and order remain those of the first-page snapshot and every ordinal appears exactly once.
  - AC: Given an unavailable or incompatible LEDGER operation or projection version, when evaluation is requested, then CLASSIFY returns a stable compatibility failure before creating an evaluation outcome.
  - AC: Given an expired or invalid snapshot cursor before complete projection acquisition, when evaluation continues, then CLASSIFY returns a stable stale-input failure and publishes no partial evaluation.
  - AC: Given transactions across accounts that contribute to one shared budget pool, when CLASSIFY evaluates them, then category identity remains cross-account and no per-account budget envelope or classifier rule set is inferred; account.id is inspected only when an explicit rule condition states that descriptor meaning differs.
  - AC: Given active transfer principal or linked-refund state, when eligibility is determined, then CLASSIFY consumes the Ledger-owned relationship outcome and never reconstructs transfer or refund linkage from description evidence.

## Depends On
- bd-8uew (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-EVALUATION-WORKFLOW): The UC verifies the complete evaluation slice.
- bd-2q0i (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-INT-LEDGER-CONTRACT): Consumes an interface produced by TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-INT-LEDGER-CONTRACT.
- bd-3g6y (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-INT-PUBLIC-CONTRACT): The UC executes through the complete published CLASSIFY contract.

## In Scope
Validation-only UC task with no implements refs; it traces UC-CLASSIFY-001 main outcomes and all four failure paths through the published boundary.

- VerifiedClassifyUc001

title: Delete one unreferenced report payload safely
description:
## Objective
DeleteInsightReportCommand removes only an unreferenced target payload and outgoing link atomically while preserving surviving Restatement chains and attributable deletion evidence.

## Implements
- FR-INSIGHTS-REPORT-DELETION: Delete retained report payloads dependency-safely
  - AC: Given a retained leaf Report Snapshot and a valid actor, reason, idempotency identity, and explicit report identity, when Delete succeeds, then its report payload and Restatement link are removed atomically.
  - AC: Given successful deletion, when the Deletion Event is inspected, then report identity, actor, reason, trusted time, idempotency outcome, and dependency result are present and no financial value or report content remains.
  - AC: Given a Report Snapshot referenced by a surviving Restatement, when Delete is requested, then dependency conflict is returned and no payload or link changes.
  - AC: Given a Restatement chain, when the owner deletes reports from leaves to root, then each unreferenced target can be deleted independently and surviving predecessors remain immutable until targeted.
  - AC: Given an unknown report identity, when Delete is requested, then Not Found is returned and no Deletion Event is created.
  - AC: Given an already deleted report and semantically identical idempotent Delete retry, when retried, then the prior logical deletion result is returned and no second event is created.
  - AC: Given no explicit Delete request, when time passes or report limits are approached, then INSIGHTS performs no automatic expiry, cleanup, or payload deletion.
  - AC: Given deletion after a backup was created, when the delete result is returned, then it states that existing point-in-time backups are unchanged and an explicit restore may reinstate their captured state.

## Depends On
- bd-7kn (TASK-INSIGHTS-STATE-FOUNDATION): Delete uses snapshot, link, payload, and event tables.
- bd-2nv (TASK-INSIGHTS-IDEMPOTENCY-EXECUTOR): Delete retries must resolve without a second event.

## In Scope
- Implement explicit replay-safe RESTRICT leaf deletion with one metadata-only DeletionEvent and no automatic cleanup.
- Produce: DeleteInsightReportCommand
- Produce: Dependency-safe deletion tests

## Out of Scope
- No sibling handoff beyond the explicit Depends On and Failure Criteria contracts.

## Success Criteria
- Delete requires explicit snapshot identity, trusted P1 actor, non-blank reason, and idempotency identity; unknown target returns NotFound and creates no event.
- A target referenced by any surviving child returns DependencyConflict and changes no payload, link, event, or replay outcome.
- A leaf deletion atomically removes its canonical payload and outgoing predecessor link and appends one DeletionEvent containing identities, actor, reason, trusted time, dependency result, and replay reference but no amount, explanation, or report content.
- Leaves can be deleted toward the root while each surviving predecessor remains immutable; exact retry of an already deleted target returns the prior metadata-only result and creates no second event.
- Existing backups remain unchanged and the result states an explicit restore may reinstate their captured state; time and limits never trigger automatic deletion.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do NOT cascade-delete referenced predecessors, delete descendants, rewrite chains, return deleted payloads, or create an event for NotFound — per ADR-CORE-0020 and DD-INSIGHTS-RETENTION-RESTATEMENT-LIFECYCLE.
- ❌ Do NOT add automatic expiry, retention cleanup, background jobs, or backup mutation.
- ❌ Do NOT split payload, link, event, and replay changes across transactions or log deleted report content.

## Approach
Implement explicit replay-safe RESTRICT leaf deletion with one metadata-only DeletionEvent and no automatic cleanup.
- Constraint: Deletion remains explicit, leaf-only, attributable, idempotent, and metadata-only.
- Expected output: DeleteInsightReportCommand
- Expected output: Dependency-safe deletion tests

title: Account for evidence states and render explanations
description:
## Objective
Every requested catalogue kind has exactly one evidence state and an explanation that cites the evaluated rule, provenance, permitted next action, and limitations.

## Implements
- FR-INSIGHTS-EVIDENCE-STATE-ACCOUNTING: Account for every evidence state
  - AC: Given a requested metric or signal kind, when a complete report is returned, then exactly one Supported, Unavailable, Insufficient Evidence, Not Started, or Deferred state accounts for it.
  - AC: Given No Budget Plan, No Active Budget Plan Revision, Unsupported Policy, Insufficient Horizon, Incomplete Coverage, Incomparable Baseline, or Not Started, when the state is returned, then the reason is a stable typed value with cited evidence and policy version.
  - AC: Given an unavailable or insufficient derived signal, when exact metrics remain supported, then the complete report preserves those exact metrics and records the signal-local state.
  - AC: Given a signal-local unavailable state, when amounts are inspected, then zero, baseline, confidence, or severity values are absent unless zero is the exact supported observed metric.
  - AC: Given cross-source incoherence, contract incompatibility, integrity failure, exact-arithmetic failure, or incomplete pagination, when generation is attempted, then no Insight Report is returned.
  - AC: Given multiple requested kinds, when report accounting is inspected, then every kind appears exactly once in deterministic catalogue order and no unsupported kind disappears silently.
- FR-INSIGHTS-REPORT-EXPLANATION: Explain report evidence deterministically
  - AC: Given a supported exact metric, when its explanation is inspected, then exact value, window bounds, category or total identity, source evidence references, and arithmetic rule are returned.
  - AC: Given a supported Linear Pace state, when its explanation is inspected, then formula version, elapsed and total days, exact plan and actual inputs, exact comparison result, and uniform-distribution limitation are returned.
  - AC: Given an unavailable, insufficient, not-started, or deferred state, when its explanation is inspected, then the typed reason, evaluated evidence, unmet rule, and permitted next action are returned without an invented result.
  - AC: Given a retained Report Snapshot identity, when Get or Explain is requested, then the exact immutable stored explanation and provenance are returned rather than recomputing current evidence.
  - AC: Given an unknown retained identity, when Get or Explain is requested, then Not Found is returned without leaking other report metadata.

title: Implement trusted Johannesburg Analysis Windows
description:
## Objective
AnalysisWindowPolicy returns the exact approved calendar bounds or a named NotStarted or Unsupported state without implicit clocks or locale behavior.

## Implements
- FR-INSIGHTS-TRUSTED-ANALYSIS-WINDOWS: Apply trusted calendar Analysis Windows
  - AC: Given any report generation, when processing starts, then one trusted TimeProvider instant is frozen before producer reads and returned as the As-of Instant in Source Provenance.
  - AC: Given any As-of Instant, when its local date is derived, then the fixed IANA timezone Africa/Johannesburg is used and host locale is ignored.
  - AC: Given a day window, when its bounds are returned, then it contains the single As-of local calendar date intersected with the selected Budget Period.
  - AC: Given a week window, when its bounds are returned, then it begins Monday, ends Sunday, and is clipped to the selected Budget Period.
  - AC: Given a month-to-date window, when its bounds are returned, then it begins on the Budget Period start and ends on the earlier of the As-of local date or period end, inclusive.
  - AC: Given a Budget Period completed before the As-of local date, when the month window is returned, then the full Budget Period is selected.
  - AC: Given a Budget Period starting after the As-of local date, when elapsed-time metrics are requested, then Not Started is returned and no zero-spend or pace interpretation is fabricated.
  - AC: Given a rolling-day or rolling-week policy request, when it is validated, then Unsupported Analysis Window is returned before financial processing.
  - AC: Given transaction membership in any window, when actuals are grouped, then LEDGER Effective Date controls membership and posting time or invocation time does not move a transaction between dates.
  - AC: Given a historical Budget Period, when a report is generated now, then the report states that current corrected producer evidence was used and does not claim to reconstruct the source state that existed at a past As-of Instant.

## Depends On
- bd-1qz (TASK-INSIGHTS-CONTRACT-MODELS): The policy returns AnalysisWindow and named evidence-state contracts.

## In Scope
- Derive deterministic inclusive day, Monday-week, and month-to-date windows from one frozen TimeProvider instant and Budget Period.
- Produce: AnalysisWindowPolicy
- Produce: Calendar conformance tests

## Out of Scope
- No sibling handoff beyond the explicit Depends On and Failure Criteria contracts.

## Success Criteria
- The caller freezes TimeProvider.GetUtcNow once before producer reads and AnalysisWindowPolicy converts it with fixed IANA Africa/Johannesburg independent of host locale.
- Day is the As-of local date intersected with the Budget Period; week is Monday through Sunday clipped to the period; month-to-date is period start through the earlier of local As-of date or period end, inclusive.
- A completed historical period returns the full period, a future period returns NotStarted with no zero-spend interpretation, and rolling-day or rolling-week requests fail before financial processing.
- Window membership uses LEDGER Effective Date and historical generation states that current corrected evidence was used rather than claiming source-state reconstruction.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do NOT accept a caller-supplied historical As-of Instant — rejected per DD-INSIGHTS-TRUSTED-WINDOW-PACE-POLICY.
- ❌ Do NOT use host locale, posting time, invocation time per member, rolling windows, or inferred daily/weekly sub-budgets.
- ❌ Do NOT read TimeProvider more than once for one report or hide NotStarted as an empty successful window.

## Approach
Derive deterministic inclusive day, Monday-week, and month-to-date windows from one frozen TimeProvider instant and Budget Period.
- Constraint: Use DateOnly boundaries and explicit inclusive semantics.
- Expected output: AnalysisWindowPolicy
- Expected output: Calendar conformance tests

## Interfaces
- Produces: AnalysisWindowPolicy.Evaluate (DM-INSIGHTS-ANALYTICAL-EVIDENCE) — ordered window bounds and named states

title: Consume the public BUDGET insight evidence operation
description:
## Objective
INSIGHTS invokes exactly one compatible budget.insights.evidence.get operation through the shared executor and exposes its typed result without private or mutation access.

## Implements
- FR-INSIGHTS-COHERENT-PUBLIC-EVIDENCE: Bind one coherent public evidence set
  - AC: Given a valid Budget Period with a selected plan revision, when evidence is bound, then the immutable plan identity, revision status, exact entries, exact totals, category lifecycle evidence, and contract provenance come from the released BUDGET read contract.
  - AC: Given a valid Budget Period with no Budget Plan, when evidence is bound, then No Budget Plan is explicit and no invented plan, zero plan, or Not Found result is substituted.
  - AC: Given a valid Budget Period with a plan but no Active revision and no explicit revision selector, when evidence is bound, then No Active Budget Plan Revision is explicit and no revision is inferred.
  - AC: Given date-granular actual evidence, when it is consumed, then every page belongs to one public snapshot or authoritative state binding and every ordinal is present exactly once.
  - AC: Given a complete evidence set with a Budget Position, when actual members are reconciled, then each member is assigned exactly once to Budgeted, Zero Budget, Unbudgeted, or Uncategorized and every exact bucket and total equals the cited Budget Position.
  - AC: Given a correction or producer write concurrent with evidence acquisition, when one coherent state cannot be proven, then generation returns Source State Changed and emits no Insight Report or Report Snapshot.
  - AC: Given cursor expiry, missing or duplicate ordinal, incompatible version, stale generation, unknown category identity, or reconciliation mismatch, when evidence binding fails, then no partial report or retained state is produced.
  - AC: Given CLASSIFY coverage is incomplete, when evidence is bound, then current LEDGER category allocation is used and Uncategorized Spend remains explicit without a direct CLASSIFY call.
  - AC: Given evidence acquisition, when dependency boundaries are inspected, then INSIGHTS invoked only released public operations, performed no upstream mutation, read no private store, and did not reproduce BUDGET position calculation.

## Depends On

## Objective

  - AC: Given identical trusted As-of Instant, normalized request values, coherent source identities, and policy versions, when generation is repeated, then semantically identical ordered content and the same content fingerprint are returned.
  - AC: Given categories, metrics, states, and explanations, when report ordering is inspected, then it follows the released deterministic ordering policy and never depends on localized display text.
  - AC: Given one report, when Source Provenance is inspected, then all producer contract versions, authoritative state or snapshot identities, plan revision, category contract, report schema, policy versions, and content fingerprints are present.
  - AC: Given a requested horizon, category count, metric count, or output size over a released limit, when validation occurs, then resource failure is returned before producer reads or report output.
  - AC: Given a successful report, when its claims are inspected, then it describes recorded Tally evidence and does not claim complete bank activity, financial advice, enforcement, or historical source reconstruction.

- Produce: InsightReportCanonicalizer

title: Verify outcome explanation and staleness
description:
## Objective
UC-CLASSIFY-002 proves bounded reproducible explanation and every specified failure without mutation or historical reconstruction.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-OUTCOME-EXPLANATION: Explain a classification outcome
  - AC: Given a retained suggestion, when its explanation is requested, then the result identifies the evaluation, transaction, category, normalization version, Rule Set Version, contributing rule versions, and allowed fields whose predicates matched.
  - AC: Given a retained no-suggestion outcome, when its explanation is requested, then the result identifies the evaluated versions and a stable no-match reason without inventing a category.
  - AC: Given a retained conflict, when its explanation is requested, then the result identifies every incompatible matching rule version and proposed category without selecting a winner.
  - AC: Given a stale outcome, when its explanation is requested, then the result identifies the fingerprint dimension that changed and states that re-evaluation is required.
  - AC: Given an unknown outcome, when explanation is requested, then CLASSIFY returns stable not-found status and does not reconstruct historical evidence from current state.
  - AC: Given a known outcome whose retained evidence is unavailable, when explanation is requested, then CLASSIFY returns stable evidence-unavailable status and does not reconstruct historical evidence from current state.
- FR-CLASSIFY-OUTCOME-INVALIDATION: Invalidate Stale Classification Outcomes
  - AC: Given a transaction becomes void in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a transaction is superseded in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.

title: Activate and retire immutable rule sets
description:
## Objective
Only current owner-approved evidence can atomically activate an immutable successor rule set; retirement and replacement preserve all prior versions.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-RULE-LIFECYCLE: Manage versioned deterministic rules
  - AC: Given a supported predicate over schema-allowed fields and an active category identifier, when a rule draft is saved, then CLASSIFY records a new immutable draft version with owner, reason, scope, normalization version, and proposed category.
  - AC: Given a rule draft is saved, when the operation completes, then no rule or Rule Set Version is activated and no LEDGER mutation occurs.
  - AC: Given an unsupported field or predicate, when a rule draft is saved, then CLASSIFY returns stable field-level validation errors and creates no activatable version.
  - AC: Given a category identifier is missing from the current catalogue, when a rule draft is saved, then CLASSIFY returns a stable category-not-found error and creates no activatable version.
  - AC: Given a category identifier is archived in the current catalogue, when a rule draft is saved, then CLASSIFY returns a stable category-inactive error and creates no activatable version.
  - AC: Given a draft whose required private validation passed, when the owner explicitly activates it, then CLASSIFY creates a new immutable active Rule Set Version containing the exact activated rule version.
  - AC: Given an active rule, when the owner retires it with a reason, then CLASSIFY creates a new active Rule Set Version without that rule and retains the retired version for inspection.
  - AC: Given an active rule that must be narrowed or replaced, when the owner activates a validated successor, then the successor references the prior version and the prior version becomes retired or superseded without in-place mutation.
  - AC: Given a category rename that preserves the same active category identifier, when rules are inspected, then their category identity is unchanged and their display name resolves to the current catalogue name.
  - AC: Given any owner decision, correction, or feedback event, when the event is recorded, then no rule version or Rule Set Version is activated automatically.
  - AC: Given a draft entered through classify.rule.save, when it is retained, then its immutable rule version records rule_origin=owner_authored and no personal rule value is compiled, seeded, logged, or exported.
  - AC: Given a draft originating from correction feedback, when it is retained, then its immutable rule version records rule_origin=feedback_derived and receives no validation, activation, broad-apply, or mutation authority from that origin.
- FR-CLASSIFY-RULE-VALIDATION: Validate candidate rule sets against private evidence
  - AC: Given a candidate normalization or Rule Set Version and an owner-only corpus, when validation starts, then the run records the candidate, corpus, expected-outcome, category-catalogue, projection-contract, and normalization fingerprints.
  - AC: Given a completed validation run, when its report is returned, then every corpus row is accounted for and aggregate totals report suggestions, no-suggestions, conflicts, stale rows, drift canaries, and incorrect-application canaries.
  - AC: Given any missing or stale required fingerprint, when activation is attempted, then CLASSIFY rejects activation without changing the active Rule Set Version.
  - AC: Given any incorrect-application canary, when activation is attempted, then CLASSIFY rejects activation without changing the active Rule Set Version.
  - AC: Given any unexplained incompatible-category conflict in required evidence, when activation is attempted, then CLASSIFY rejects activation without changing the active Rule Set Version.
  - AC: Given an unavailable private corpus, when an existing active rule set is evaluated, then CLASSIFY may use that unchanged active version.
  - AC: Given an unavailable private corpus, when a new rule or normalization version is activated, then CLASSIFY rejects activation without changing the active Rule Set Version.
  - AC: Given an unavailable private corpus, when broad-apply authorization is requested, then CLASSIFY rejects authorization before LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given a validation report, when it is persisted or exported, then it contains corpus fingerprints and aggregate outcomes but no raw transaction description, normalized token, financial value, or expected-outcome row.
  - AC: Given an owner-authored candidate rulebook, when its pre-authority gate runs, then every private row is accounted for exactly once, incorrect applications and unexplained incompatible conflicts are zero, coverage and no-suggestion totals are explicit, drift canaries and deterministic fingerprints are stable, and owner decision and time benefit are measured.
  - AC: Given owner-authored safety passes but measured benefit is insufficient for broad authority, when activation or exact-rule broad apply is considered, then CLASSIFY requires an explicit product decision and does not invent a 50 percent benefit threshold.

## Depends On

title: Wire and prove the complete CLASSIFY contract
description:
## Objective
Prove the complete installed public CLASSIFY contract.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-CONTRACT-DISCOVERY: Discover the CLASSIFY command contract
  - AC: Given a compatible Tally executable, when schema discovery is requested, then the registry exposes every operation required by C12 with its versioned input, result, error, exit, mutability, idempotency, limit, and compatibility contract.
  - AC: Given any public CLASSIFY operation, when its schema is requested repeatedly for the same contract version, then the semantic descriptor is deterministic.
  - AC: Given an unknown CLASSIFY operation, when schema or invocation is requested, then Tally returns a stable unknown-operation error and no private storage detail.
  - AC: Given contract discovery, when descriptors are returned, then no CLASSIFY store, private corpus, or LEDGER data read occurs.
- FR-CLASSIFY-STRUCTURED-INVOCATION: Invoke CLASSIFY operations non-interactively
  - AC: Given valid structured input for a public operation, when invocation completes, then exactly one versioned structured business result is written to stdout and the process exits with the documented category.
  - AC: Given an expected validation, not-found, conflict, lifecycle, stale, compatibility, resource, or downstream LEDGER failure, when invocation completes, then one module-scoped machine-readable error is returned with the documented non-zero exit.
  - AC: Given malformed input or a forbidden unknown field, when invocation is attempted, then validation fails before evaluation, rule-state change, or LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given an unsupported CLASSIFY or required LEDGER contract version, when invocation is attempted, then compatibility fails before financial data read or mutation.
  - AC: Given a mutating rule, feedback, abandon, cleanup, or apply operation, when its request lacks required actor context or idempotency identity, then CLASSIFY rejects it before mutation.
  - AC: Given any successful or expected-failure invocation, when stderr is inspected, then it contains metadata-only diagnostics and no serialized request, result, or financial payload.

## Depends On
- bd-3hcn (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-ABANDON-CLEANUP): Final wiring consumes abandon and cleanup handlers.

## In Scope

- Extend the shared `OperationDescriptor`/`OperationSchema` path so CLASSIFY descriptors carry the typed `OperationLimits` produced by `bd-3kex`; CLASSIFY limits are non-null while legacy operation limits remain absent/byte-compatible.
- Own the explicit registry inventory, runtime `classify.*` dispatch, `LedgerServices` composition slot, and `Program` descriptor-only/runtime split. Schema discovery must not initialize or read the CLASSIFY store.
- Own the process-envelope adapter for the concrete `ClassifyResultEnvelope` contract, including `correlation_ref`, while preserving existing Ledger/INGEST/BUDGET process output for non-CLASSIFY operations.

## Out of Scope

title: Implement the closed rule vocabulary
description:
## Objective
Every first-release rule is finite, canonical, deterministic, explainable, and incapable of executing arbitrary expressions.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-DETERMINISTIC-EVALUATION: Evaluate deterministic classification outcomes
  - AC: Given a complete eligible projection, active category catalogue, normalization version, and Rule Set Version, when evaluation completes, then every input ordinal has exactly one outcome of suggestion, no-suggestion, conflict, or stale and the outcome totals equal the input count.
  - AC: Given an identical Evaluation Fingerprint, when evaluation is repeated, then ordered outcomes and Match Evidence are semantically identical.
  - AC: Given exactly one matching active rule or multiple matching active rules that all propose the same active category, when a transaction is evaluated, then one suggestion names that category and every contributing rule version.
  - AC: Given active matching rules that propose different categories, when a transaction is evaluated, then the outcome is Rule Conflict with no selected category.
  - AC: Given no active matching rule, when a transaction is evaluated, then the outcome is explicit no-suggestion with no selected category.
  - AC: Given any completed evaluation, when LEDGER category history and transaction source facts are inspected, then evaluation has changed neither.
- FR-CLASSIFY-RULE-LIFECYCLE: Manage versioned deterministic rules
  - AC: Given a supported predicate over schema-allowed fields and an active category identifier, when a rule draft is saved, then CLASSIFY records a new immutable draft version with owner, reason, scope, normalization version, and proposed category.
  - AC: Given a rule draft is saved, when the operation completes, then no rule or Rule Set Version is activated and no LEDGER mutation occurs.
  - AC: Given an unsupported field or predicate, when a rule draft is saved, then CLASSIFY returns stable field-level validation errors and creates no activatable version.
  - AC: Given a category identifier is missing from the current catalogue, when a rule draft is saved, then CLASSIFY returns a stable category-not-found error and creates no activatable version.
  - AC: Given a category identifier is archived in the current catalogue, when a rule draft is saved, then CLASSIFY returns a stable category-inactive error and creates no activatable version.
  - AC: Given a draft whose required private validation passed, when the owner explicitly activates it, then CLASSIFY creates a new immutable active Rule Set Version containing the exact activated rule version.
  - AC: Given an active rule, when the owner retires it with a reason, then CLASSIFY creates a new active Rule Set Version without that rule and retains the retired version for inspection.
  - AC: Given an active rule that must be narrowed or replaced, when the owner activates a validated successor, then the successor references the prior version and the prior version becomes retired or superseded without in-place mutation.
  - AC: Given a category rename that preserves the same active category identifier, when rules are inspected, then their category identity is unchanged and their display name resolves to the current catalogue name.
  - AC: Given any owner decision, correction, or feedback event, when the event is recorded, then no rule version or Rule Set Version is activated automatically.
  - AC: Given a draft entered through classify.rule.save, when it is retained, then its immutable rule version records rule_origin=owner_authored and no personal rule value is compiled, seeded, logged, or exported.
  - AC: Given a draft originating from correction feedback, when it is retained, then its immutable rule version records rule_origin=feedback_derived and receives no validation, activation, broad-apply, or mutation authority from that origin.

## Depends On
- bd-3kex (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-CONTRACT-FOUNDATION): The vocabulary publishes descriptors through the CLASSIFY rule contracts.

## In Scope
Create the finite field/predicate registry, canonical typed conditions, and normalization v1 with source-generated descriptors.

- Canonical RuleCondition values

## Out of Scope
- bd-2sde (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-DETERMINISTIC-ENGINE) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- bd-1qb6 (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-RULE-DRAFT-SAVE) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.

## Success Criteria

- NormalizerV1 applies Unicode NFKC, invariant case folding, punctuation boundaries, and whitespace collapse while preserving digits and token order.
- Unknown fields, predicates, values, duplicate conditions, empty rules, over-length values, and invalid minor-unit ranges return stable field-level errors.
- Canonical descriptors and condition hashes are byte-stable across repeated runs and culture settings.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do not add OR, NOT, priority, regex, fuzzy, wildcard, script, plugin, arbitrary expression, or model-score behavior - rejected by DD-CLASSIFY-RULE-VOCABULARY.
- ❌ Do not remove dates, amounts, reference numbers, stop words, digits, or token order in normalization v1.
- ❌ Do not delegate rule interpretation to the AI Agent Host.

title: Abandon state and clean recognized artifacts
description:
## Objective
Unreferenced work and recognized crash residue can be removed safely while every referenced rule, apply, allocation, and feedback history remains intact.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-STATE-RETENTION-CLEANUP: Retain attributable state and clean derived artifacts
  - AC: Given an activated rule, apply result, or feedback record, when retention is inspected, then CLASSIFY retains the minimal actor, reason, timestamp, stable references, fingerprints, prior state, and resulting state required for explanation and replay.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path succeeds, when its result is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path returns an expected failure, when its result is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path returns an unexpected handled failure, when its failure is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given an unreferenced draft rule, validation run, or evaluation run, when the owner explicitly abandons it, then it becomes non-activatable and its removable derived payload is deleted without changing active rules or LEDGER.
  - AC: Given a rule version, evaluation, or apply result referenced by active state, Ledger mutation provenance, or feedback, when hard removal is requested, then CLASSIFY rejects removal and requires lifecycle retirement or retained history.
  - AC: Given process startup, when orphan temporary artifacts from a prior crash are found, then CLASSIFY validates ownership and removes only recognized CLASSIFY temporaries before accepting new mutation.
  - AC: Given cleanup completion, when status is requested, then it returns cleanup run ID, policy version, removed artifact count, retained artifact count, and per-kind counts but no removed payload or path.
