title: Publish CLASSIFY operation contracts
description:
## Objective
The Tally registry can represent every CLASSIFY request, result, error, limit, compatibility, mutability, and idempotency contract without loading private data.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-CONTRACT-DISCOVERY: Discover the CLASSIFY command contract
  - AC: Given a compatible Tally executable, when schema discovery is requested, then the registry exposes every operation required by C12 with its versioned input, result, error, exit, mutability, idempotency, limit, and compatibility contract.
  - AC: Given any public CLASSIFY operation, when its schema is requested repeatedly for the same contract version, then the semantic descriptor is deterministic.
  - AC: Given an unknown CLASSIFY operation, when schema or invocation is requested, then Tally returns a stable unknown-operation error and no private storage detail.
  - AC: Given contract discovery, when descriptors are returned, then no CLASSIFY store, private corpus, or LEDGER data read occurs.
- FR-CLASSIFY-STRUCTURED-INVOCATION: Invoke CLASSIFY operations non-interactively
  - AC: Given valid structured input for a public operation, when invocation completes, then exactly one versioned structured business result is written to stdout and the process exits with the documented category.
  - AC: Given an expected validation, not-found, conflict, lifecycle, stale, compatibility, resource, or downstream LEDGER failure, when invocation completes, then one module-scoped machine-readable error is returned with the documented non-zero exit.
  - AC: Given malformed input or a forbidden unknown field, when invocation is attempted, then validation fails before evaluation, rule-state change, or LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given an unsupported CLASSIFY or required LEDGER contract version, when invocation is attempted, then compatibility fails before financial data read or mutation.
  - AC: Given a mutating rule, feedback, abandon, cleanup, or apply operation, when its request lacks required actor context or idempotency identity, then CLASSIFY rejects it before mutation.
  - AC: Given any successful or expected-failure invocation, when stderr is inspected, then it contains metadata-only diagnostics and no serialized request, result, or financial payload.

## Depends On
- None; this is an initial ready-frontier bead.

## In Scope
Create source-generated DTOs, stable errors, descriptors, mapper boundary, and feature-local contract registration for the exact twelve operations.

- ClassifyOperationContracts
- ClassifyJsonContext
- ClassifyOperationModule descriptors
- Pure ClassifyContractMapper boundary

- Define the shared `OperationLimits` contract in `src/Tally/Contracts/Common/OperationLimits.cs` with explicit `max_transaction_count`, `max_rule_count`, `max_evidence_row_count`, `max_corpus_row_count`, `max_memory_bytes`, and `max_processing_time_ms` members. Publish exact CLASSIFY v1 values and inclusive/exclusive boundary semantics for every operation; an inapplicable dimension is explicit, never silently omitted.
- Attach a non-null, deterministic `OperationLimits` value to every one of the twelve CLASSIFY descriptors. This bead owns the limit type and exact values; shared registry/schema wiring is owned by `bd-3g6y`.

## Out of Scope
- bd-3g6y (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-INT-PUBLIC-CONTRACT) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- bd-3gmq (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-RULE-VOCABULARY) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- Do not modify files reserved by sibling beads or implement any capability outside the twelve-operation CLASSIFY v1 surface.

## Success Criteria
- The descriptor set contains exactly the twelve C12 operation IDs with deterministic versioned request, result, error, exit, mutability, idempotency, limit, and compatibility metadata.
- Source-generated JSON rejects unknown fields; malformed, incompatible, missing-actor, and missing-idempotency requests fail before a handler effect.
- Complex input is accepted only through explicit stdin or file JSON and sensitive paths never appear in process arguments.
- Descriptor discovery and unknown-operation handling perform no CLASSIFY, private corpus, or Ledger data read.

- Every descriptor publishes a non-null deterministic limits object with the exact transaction, rule, evidence-row, corpus-row, memory, and processing-time limits required by C11/NFR-CLASSIFY-BOUNDED-EVALUATION; exact-limit acceptance and one-over-limit rejection are represented in the contract.
- The limit metadata is a typed versioned contract consumed by the shared registry, not prose, a zero placeholder, or a second undiscoverable CLASSIFY schema.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do not merge capabilities behind generic invoke, manage, run, save, update, list, or delete discriminators - rejected by DD-CLASSIFY-CLI-OPERATION-CONTRACT.
- ❌ Do not add HTTP endpoints, FastEndpoints, reflection scanning, a mediator, or an event bus - rejected by DD-CLASSIFY-APPLICATION-ARCHITECTURE.
- ❌ Do not serialize private payloads to stdout errors, stderr, logs, or crash diagnostics.
- ❌ Do not use strings for system-owned operation state when a closed enum is defined - per ADR-CORE-0004.

- ❌ Do not leave limits in prose, use `0` as an unknown-limit sentinel, or publish a parallel descriptor surface that `schema list/show` cannot discover.

## Approach
Create source-generated DTOs, stable errors, descriptors, mapper boundary, and feature-local contract registration for the exact twelve operations.

Constraints:
- Reuse OperationRegistry, OperationDescriptor, CommandResult, and process envelopes produced by the Ledger core task.

Expected outputs:
- ClassifyOperationContracts
- ClassifyJsonContext

- Pure ClassifyContractMapper boundary

- Treat `OperationLimits` as a typed common contract with stable JSON names and deterministic units. The descriptor module supplies the exact CLASSIFY values; `bd-3g6y` extends the shared registry/schema without duplicating those values.

## Interfaces

- Produces: ClassifyJsonContext (DM-CLASSIFY-OPERATION-CONTRACTS)

title: Support recursive parent-category budget envelopes
description:
Problem: budget.position.get in Tally 0.3.0 matches plan entries only to exact category IDs. A transaction classified to a nested child is reported unbudgeted even when an ancestor carries the intended shared envelope. This prevents detailed classifications such as Health & wellness and Physiotherapy from consuming a shared Medical expenses budget.

Desired behavior:
- Resolve each categorized actual recursively from its exact category toward the root.
- The nearest explicit plan entry wins.
- A child allocation overrides an ancestor allocation for that child subtree.
- An explicit zero-budget child is still an allocation and blocks fallback to its parent.
- If no category in the ancestry has a plan entry, classify the actual as unbudgeted.
- Count every actual exactly once; do not double-count child spend in both child and parent rows.
- Parent rows aggregate direct actuals plus descendant actuals not captured by a nearer child allocation.
- Preserve deterministic snapshot/provenance behavior across category reparenting and historical queries.
- Expose enough position provenance for clients to report the effective budget category used for a child transaction.

Acceptance coverage:
1. Parent-only allocation with direct and multi-level descendant actuals.
2. Mixed parent and child allocations where nearest allocation wins.
3. Explicit zero-budget child overriding a funded parent.
4. Unbudgeted fallback when no ancestor is funded.
5. Refunds/credits, archived categories, reparenting, arithmetic overflow, and reconciliation invariants.
6. Existing exact-category behavior remains unchanged for flat taxonomies.
7. Budget-position totals reconcile and no actual is counted more than once.
close_reason: All envelope chain beads closed (bd-1xlf, bd-tuey, bd-3uzt, bd-113k, bd-zsby): nearest-ancestor resolution, integrity, provenance, and reparent re-lensing verified under fast gate.

title: Append explicit Restatements and deterministic differences
description:
## Objective
RestateInsightReportCommand creates one immutable child only when provenance, version, schema, or semantic content changes and returns ordered bounded differences.

## Implements
- FR-INSIGHTS-REPORT-RESTATEMENT: Create an explicit linked Restatement
  - AC: Given an existing compatible Report Snapshot and a valid actor-attributed idempotent Restate request, when current coherent evidence is available, then one new Report Snapshot is generated without modifying the predecessor.
  - AC: Given a successful Restatement, when its provenance is inspected, then exactly one predecessor identity and the new current source and policy identities are explicit.
  - AC: Given predecessor and restated reports, when the difference result is returned, then Source Provenance, policy-version, exact-metric, signal-state, explanation, and Attention Item differences are separated and deterministically ordered.
  - AC: Given identical predecessor source identities, policy versions, and semantic content, when Restate is requested, then No Change is returned and no new Report Snapshot is created.
  - AC: Given any changed producer state or snapshot identity, policy version, report schema version, or semantic report content, when Restate succeeds, then one new linked Report Snapshot is retained even when exact metric values remain equal.
  - AC: Given an unknown, deleted, corrupted, or incompatible predecessor, when Restate is requested, then the exact stable failure is returned and no new report is created.
  - AC: Given unavailable or incoherent current evidence, when Restate is requested, then no partial Restatement or difference payload is retained.
  - AC: Given the same idempotency identity and same normalized Restate request, when retried, then the prior logical outcome is returned without a second Restatement.

## Depends On
- bd-7kn (TASK-INSIGHTS-STATE-FOUNDATION): Restate reads verified predecessors and atomically writes child and link rows.
- bd-2nv (TASK-INSIGHTS-IDEMPOTENCY-EXECUTOR): Restate resolves replay before current producer access.
- bd-1cr (TASK-INSIGHTS-GENERATE-REPORT): Restate reuses the approved current report path.

## In Scope
- Implement replay-safe current-evidence generation, predecessor comparison, NoChange, and atomic linked snapshot creation without rewriting history.
- Produce: InsightReportDiffer
- Produce: RestateInsightReportCommand
- Produce: Restatement and NoChange tests

## Out of Scope
- No sibling handoff beyond the explicit Depends On and Failure Criteria contracts.

## Success Criteria
- Restate requires one compatible existing predecessor plus actor, reason, normalized selectors, and idempotency; unknown, deleted, corrupt, or incompatible predecessors fail before producer access.
- Exact replay resolves before current evidence; a new request generates through the existing Generate path and never changes the predecessor.
- InsightReportDiffer compares source identities, policy versions, report schema, exact metrics, evidence states, explanations, and deferred Attention Item collection in fixed section and item order.
- Identical source identities, versions, schema, and semantic content return NoChange and store only the replay outcome; any changed source, version, schema, or content appends one child snapshot and one predecessor link atomically even when visible amounts remain equal.
- Current-evidence, comparison, cancellation, or write failure returns no partial difference, snapshot, link, or successful outcome; same-key replay never creates a second Restatement.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do NOT update or silently replace the predecessor, auto-restate after corrections, store arbitrary caller reports, or event-source every calculation — rejected per DD-INSIGHTS-RETENTION-RESTATEMENT-LIFECYCLE.
- ❌ Do NOT compare display text, omit provenance/version-only changes, expose unrelated transactions, or store a difference without its complete child snapshot.
- ❌ Do NOT duplicate the Generate pipeline or call producer operations after an exact replay is found.

## Approach
Implement replay-safe current-evidence generation, predecessor comparison, NoChange, and atomic linked snapshot creation without rewriting history.
- Constraint: One child has exactly one predecessor; a predecessor may have multiple surviving children.
- Expected output: InsightReportDiffer
- Expected output: RestateInsightReportCommand
- Expected output: Restatement and NoChange tests

## Interfaces
- Consumes: GenerateInsightReportQuery.HandleAsync (DM-INSIGHTS-INSIGHT-REPORT) — current complete evidence
- Consumes: InsightsIdempotencyExecutor.ExecuteAsync (DM-INSIGHTS-IDEMPOTENCY) — replay before producer access
- Consumes: InsightsStateStore (DM-INSIGHTS-STATE-STORE) — predecessor read and atomic child/link append
- Produces: InsightReportDiffer.Compare (DM-INSIGHTS-RETAINED-REPORT-LIFECYCLE) — ordered bounded differences
- Produces: RestateInsightReportCommand.HandleAsync (DM-INSIGHTS-OPERATION-CONTRACTS) — insights.report.restate handler

## Files (reservation globs)
- `src/Tally/Domain/Insights/Reports/InsightReportDiffer.cs` (create) — deterministic bounded report comparison
- `src/Tally/Features/Insights/History/Restate/RestateInsightReportCommand.cs` (create) — replay-safe linked restatement handler
- `tests/Tally.Tests/Insights/History/RestateInsightReportCommandTests.cs` (test) — predecessor, difference, NoChange, replay, and atomicity tests

## Verification
- **Build:** `dotnet build`
- **Test:** `dotnet test tests/Tally.Tests/Tally.Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~RestateInsightReportCommandTests` — exit 0; at least 22 unknown, deleted, corrupt, incompatible, replay-before-read, no-change, source-only, policy-only, schema-only, equal-amount semantic-change, ordered-difference, cancellation, write, crash, predecessor-immutability, and duplicate-prevention cases are discovered and 0 fail

title: Record bounded correction feedback
description:
## Objective
Owner acceptance, rejection, and correction remain attributable and may suggest a bounded draft without rewriting history, broadening, or activating automatically.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-CORRECTION-FEEDBACK: Turn owner corrections into bounded feedback
  - AC: Given an accepted or rejected outcome, when feedback is recorded, then it references the exact transaction, evaluation, outcome, normalization, rule-set, and contributing rule versions plus owner actor, reason, and timestamp.
  - AC: Given a category correction completed in LEDGER, when CLASSIFY records feedback, then it references the authoritative prior and resulting Ledger allocations without rewriting either.
  - AC: Given one correction, when CLASSIFY derives a response, then it records no proposal or one smallest-scope retire, narrow, or replacement proposal.
  - AC: Given a feedback-derived proposal, when it is recorded, then CLASSIFY does not activate the proposal automatically.
  - AC: Given a feedback-derived proposal, when it is recorded, then CLASSIFY does not broaden an existing rule automatically.
  - AC: Given a feedback-derived candidate, when activation is requested, then the same private validation and explicit activation requirements as any other candidate apply.
  - AC: Given historical feedback, when a rule is retired or superseded, then the feedback remains attributable to the original rule version and outcome.
  - AC: Given unavailable prior Match Evidence, when feedback is recorded, then CLASSIFY stores the owner decision but creates no rule proposal from reconstructed current evidence.
  - AC: Given an accepted or rejected suggestion, when feedback is recorded, then CLASSIFY may record no proposal and never invents a rule change merely because the owner accepted or rejected one outcome.
  - AC: Given a transaction-specific correction, when feedback is recorded, then the authoritative transaction correction remains separate from every reusable rule draft and is never generalized from that row without the normal save, validation, and activation path.

title: Resolve each Budget Actual to its nearest ancestor Category Budget Entry
description:
## Objective
Each Budget Actual is assigned to exactly one position through nearest-ancestor resolution, and every row reports a direct/descendant partition that sums to its own total.

## Implements
- FR-BUDGET-POSITION-QUERY: Calculate exact Budget Positions
  - AC: Given a Category Budget Entry on a parent Spend Category and Budget Actuals assigned to that parent directly and to descendant Spend Categories one and two levels below that carry no entry, when the position is calculated, then every one of those Budget Actuals appears exactly once in the parent Budgeted position, and that row reports the direct subtotal, the descendant subtotal, and the absorbed descendant Spend Category identifiers in ascending ordinal order.
  - AC: Given Category Budget Entries on both a parent Spend Category and one of its descendants, when the position is calculated, then a Budget Actual assigned at or below the descendant appears exactly once in the descendant position and is excluded from the parent position, while a Budget Actual under the parent outside the descendant subtree appears exactly once in the parent position.
  - AC: Given a Category Budget Entry with Planned Spend equal to zero on a descendant Spend Category whose ancestor carries Planned Spend greater than zero, when the position is calculated, then Budget Actuals at or below that descendant appear exactly once in the descendant Zero Budget Position and no part of them falls back to the funded ancestor.
  - AC: Given any selected revision and LEDGER snapshot, when every category position is returned, then each row's actual value equals the exact sum of its direct actual value and its descendant actual value, and the sum across all rows plus Uncategorized Spend equals the membership total, so no Budget Actual is counted more than once.
  - AC: Given a Budget Plan Revision whose Spend Categories are all root nodes with no descendants, when the position is calculated, then every value, bucket, ordering, and total is identical to the `budget-position-v1` exact-identity result for the same inputs.
  - AC: Given Budget Actuals on two distinct Spend Categories whose shared ancestry carries no Category Budget Entry, when the position is calculated, then each produces its own Unbudgeted Spend row whose direct actual equals its row actual, whose descendant actual is exactly zero, and whose absorbed identifier list is empty, and no aggregated ancestor row is produced.

## Depends On
- bd-1xlf (TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-CONTRACTS): Resolution writes the partition fields that bead adds to CategoryPosition.
- bd-tuey (TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-ANCESTRY-COMPOSITION): Resolution reads AncestryIds, populated only once the mapper carries it from the snapshot.

## In Scope
- Nearest-ancestor scan from the final ancestry index toward index zero
- Per-row direct and descendant partition with AbsorbedCategoryIds
- EffectiveCategoryId populated per Budget Actual member

## Out of Scope
- Ancestry validation, overflow, refund-sign and archived-ancestor proofs — bd-113k (TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-INTEGRITY)
- Published-contract provenance and reparent proofs — bd-zsby (TASK-BUDGET-GATE-INT-ENVELOPE-PROVENANCE)

## Success Criteria
- Given a Category Budget Entry on a parent Spend Category and Budget Actuals on that parent plus descendants one and two levels below carrying no entry, when the position is calculated, then all of them appear exactly once in the parent Budgeted position, its direct actual equals only the parent-assigned Budget Actual, its descendant actual equals the sum of the two descendants, and its absorbed identifier list names both descendants in ascending ordinal order.
- Given Category Budget Entries on both a parent Spend Category and its descendant, when the position is calculated, then a Budget Actual at or below the descendant appears exactly once in the descendant position and is excluded from the parent position.
- Given a Category Budget Entry with Planned Spend equal to zero on a descendant whose ancestor has Planned Spend greater than zero, when the position is calculated, then Budget Actuals at or below that descendant appear exactly once in the descendant Zero Budget Position and the funded ancestor Remaining value is unreduced by them.
- Given a Budget Actual whose frozen ancestry carries no Category Budget Entry at any element, when the position is calculated, then it appears exactly once as Unbudgeted Spend keyed by its exact assigned Spend Category identifier, with direct actual equal to the row actual, descendant actual exactly zero, and an empty absorbed identifier list.
- Given arbitrary Spend Category trees, arbitrary Category Budget Entry placements including zero amounts, and arbitrary Budget Actual assignments, when each position is calculated, then every row actual equals its direct actual plus its descendant actual and the sum of all row actuals plus Uncategorized Spend equals the membership total.
- Given a Budget Plan Revision whose Spend Categories are all root nodes, when the position is calculated, then every bucket, ordering, value, and total equals the exact-identity result for the same inputs and every descendant actual is exactly zero.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do NOT freeze ancestry at classification time or persist any historical ancestry in BUDGET — rejected alternative A in DD-BUDGET-CATEGORY-ENVELOPE-RESOLUTION, because it needs a LEDGER storage change and contradicts OQ-BUDGET-8 and A4.
- ❌ Do NOT add DescendantActualMinorUnits on top of ActualMinorUnits — the partition composes the row total exactly, per DD-BUDGET-CATEGORY-ENVELOPE-RESOLUTION.
- ❌ Do NOT let an Unbudgeted Spend row absorb descendants — only rows produced by a Category Budget Entry absorb, per DD-BUDGET-CATEGORY-ENVELOPE-RESOLUTION.
- ❌ Do NOT persist any position, actual, cursor, or report state — per DD-BUDGET-EXACT-POSITION-CALCULATION the calculator stays pure.
- ❌ Do NOT weaken or remove the existing assertion that bucket actual subtotals reconcile to the membership total — it is the exactly-once proof, per DD-BUDGET-EXACT-POSITION-CALCULATION.
- ❌ Do NOT use unchecked arithmetic for any new sum — overflow returns the stable integrity failure with no partial result.

## Approach
- The calculator performs no I/O, no storage access, and no LEDGER call.
- Ancestry is scanned from the final index toward index zero; the first element carrying a Category Budget Entry wins.
- Int64 checked addition, subtraction, and magnitude operations for every amount.
- Resolution replaces the existing exact-category key lookup inside the plan-entry loop; the surrounding exhaustive-assignment structure, ordering, and reconciliation assertion stay unchanged.

Expected outputs:
- Nearest-ancestor envelope resolution in the pure calculator
- Per-row direct and descendant partition with absorbed identifier list
- Ancestry validation returning the stable integrity failure

## Interfaces

title: Prove owner-rulebook safety before classification authority
description:
## Objective
Prove that an owner-authored deterministic rulebook is safe, deterministic, useful, and privacy-preserving before any rule can become active or any CLASSIFY apply workflow can gain authority.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-RULE-VALIDATION: Validate candidate rule sets against private evidence
  - AC: Given a candidate normalization or Rule Set Version and an owner-only corpus, when validation starts, then the run records the candidate, corpus, expected-outcome, category-catalogue, projection-contract, and normalization fingerprints.
  - AC: Given a completed validation run, when its report is returned, then every corpus row is accounted for and aggregate totals report suggestions, no-suggestions, conflicts, stale rows, drift canaries, and incorrect-application canaries.
  - AC: Given any missing or stale required fingerprint, when activation is attempted, then CLASSIFY rejects activation without changing the active Rule Set Version.
  - AC: Given any incorrect-application canary, when activation is attempted, then CLASSIFY rejects activation without changing the active Rule Set Version.
  - AC: Given any unexplained incompatible-category conflict in required evidence, when activation is attempted, then CLASSIFY rejects activation without changing the active Rule Set Version.
  - AC: Given an unavailable private corpus, when an existing active rule set is evaluated, then CLASSIFY may use that unchanged active version.
  - AC: Given an unavailable private corpus, when a new rule or normalization version is activated, then CLASSIFY rejects activation without changing the active Rule Set Version.
  - AC: Given an unavailable private corpus, when broad-apply authorization is requested, then CLASSIFY rejects authorization before LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given a validation report, when it is persisted or exported, then it contains corpus fingerprints and aggregate outcomes but no raw transaction description, normalized token, financial value, or expected-outcome row.
  - AC: Given an owner-authored candidate rulebook, when its pre-authority gate runs, then every private row is accounted for exactly once, incorrect applications and unexplained incompatible conflicts are zero, coverage and no-suggestion totals are explicit, drift canaries and deterministic fingerprints are stable, and owner decision and time benefit are measured.
  - AC: Given owner-authored safety passes but measured benefit is insufficient for broad authority, when activation or exact-rule broad apply is considered, then CLASSIFY requires an explicit product decision and does not invent a 50 percent benefit threshold.

## Depends On
- bd-2sde (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-DETERMINISTIC-ENGINE): The candidate rulebook must exercise the production deterministic engine.
- bd-2olb (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-LEDGER-CLASSIFICATION-CLIENT): Evidence must come through the public Ledger projection client.
- bd-2fdz (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-PRIVATE-CORPUS-READER): The owner-only corpus boundary must be enforced.
- bd-2kpw (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-RULE-VALIDATION): The gate must exercise the real rule validation lifecycle.

## In Scope
Run the owner-confirmed candidate rulebook against an owner-only representative post-INGEST 90-day corpus and temporal hold-out through the public LEDGER classification projection. Emit aggregate-only evidence and block activation, apply authority, and module completion unless every safety gate passes. Coverage, no-suggestion, owner-decision, and timing benefit are reported; insufficient benefit requires an explicit product decision and is not replaced by an invented percentage threshold.

- Aggregate-only VerifiedOwnerRulebookGateReceipt
- Conformance script and private-boundary operator guide

## Out of Scope
- bd-1yaj (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-GRAPH-QUALITY) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- bd-2igu (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-SECURITY) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- bd-3e6o (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-RULE-ACTIVATION-LIFECYCLE) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- Do not modify files reserved by sibling beads or implement any capability outside the twelve-operation CLASSIFY v1 surface.

## Success Criteria
- Validate the owner-only saved rulebook with the production validator, public LEDGER projection, and untracked representative 90-day corpus plus hold-out; never compile, seed, log, export, or commit personal values.
- Account for every row across eligible, suggested, correction, no-suggestion, conflict, excluded, and stale totals; exercise mixed, sign, account, fee, transfer, refund, and shared-medical canaries.
- Require zero incorrect applications, unexplained conflicts, unauthorized mutations, or description-inferred relationships; identical inputs are deterministic and drift canaries pass.
- Report aggregate-only coverage, no-suggestion, owner-decision, and elapsed-time evidence. Safety failure blocks authority; insufficient benefit requires an explicit owner decision, never an invented percentage.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Block activation, apply, command completion, and module completion on any safety, accounting, conflict, determinism, drift, privacy, or Ledger-truth failure.
- ❌ Never disclose private payloads or paths; infer Ledger state; discover or seed rules; broaden grammar; add an evaluator; weaken conflicts; or treat coverage as authority.

## Approach
Run the owner-confirmed candidate rulebook against an owner-only representative post-INGEST 90-day corpus and temporal hold-out through the public LEDGER classification projection. Emit aggregate-only evidence and block activation, apply authority, and module completion unless every safety gate passes. Coverage, no-suggestion, owner-decision, and timing benefit are reported; insufficient benefit requires an explicit product decision and is not replaced by an invented percentage threshold.

## Hermes architecture-contract amendment (2026-08-01)
- No thirteenth CLASSIFY operation and no second evaluator. The gate invokes existing public `classify.rule.validate`.
- Owner inputs are explicit candidate rule-version IDs, representative corpus, temporal hold-out, and aggregate decision/time evidence; missing input yields a stable blocked receipt.

title: Retain an internally generated immutable report
description:
## Objective
RetainInsightReportCommand appends exactly one complete immutable ReportSnapshot and replay outcome without accepting caller-authored report content.

## Implements
- FR-INSIGHTS-REPORT-RETENTION: Retain an immutable Report Snapshot explicitly
  - AC: Given an ordinary Generate request, when it succeeds, then no Report Snapshot, idempotency outcome, or retained payload is created.
  - AC: Given a valid Retain request with analysis inputs, actor, reason, and idempotency identity, when it succeeds, then INSIGHTS generates one complete report and atomically appends one immutable Report Snapshot.
  - AC: Given a Retain request, when input is validated, then no arbitrary caller-authored report payload is accepted as the stored result.
  - AC: Given a retained snapshot, when its identity is inspected, then actor, reason, trusted creation time, analysis request fingerprint, source and policy versions, content fingerprint, and report schema version are present.
  - AC: Given the same idempotency identity and semantically identical normalized request, when Retain is retried, then the prior logical Report Snapshot is returned and no duplicate is created.
  - AC: Given the same idempotency identity with different normalized input, when Retain is attempted, then conflict is returned and retained history is unchanged.
  - AC: Given validation, generation, persistence, cancellation, or crash failure, when Retain ends, then no partial Report Snapshot or successful idempotency outcome exists.
  - AC: Given later source corrections or policy changes, when a retained snapshot is read, then its stored content and fingerprint remain unchanged.

## Depends On
- bd-7kn (TASK-INSIGHTS-STATE-FOUNDATION): Retain writes the snapshot and payload schema.
- bd-2nv (TASK-INSIGHTS-IDEMPOTENCY-EXECUTOR): Retain must resolve and reserve replay before producer access.
- bd-1cr (TASK-INSIGHTS-GENERATE-REPORT): Retain reuses the complete approved generation path.

## In Scope
- Implement the explicit owner-attributed idempotent Retain slice over the ephemeral Generate path and one atomic store transaction.
- Produce: RetainInsightReportCommand
- Produce: Atomic retained-generation tests

## Out of Scope
- No sibling handoff beyond the explicit Depends On and Failure Criteria contracts.

## Success Criteria
- Retain requires normalized analysis input, trusted P1 actor, non-blank reason, and idempotency identity and accepts no report payload, reportId, snapshotId, contentFingerprint, or provenance authored by the caller.
- Exact replay resolves before TimeProvider and producer access; a new request invokes the existing Generate path, allocates one opaque ULID snapshotId, and appends snapshot metadata, canonical report payload, fingerprint, actor, reason, and Succeeded outcome in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction.
- The retained identity records analysis-request fingerprint, source and policy versions, report schema, content fingerprint, trusted creation time, actor, and reason; later producer or policy change cannot alter it.
- Changed-input replay conflicts; validation, generation, cancellation, SQLite, disk, or commit failure leaves no partial snapshot, payload, or successful replay outcome.
- Logs and errors contain only safe stable IDs, fingerprints, states, and counts.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do NOT retain ordinary Generate results automatically, accept caller-authored report content, update an existing report, or store upstream member rows — rejected per DD-INSIGHTS-RETENTION-RESTATEMENT-LIFECYCLE.
- ❌ Do NOT split snapshot, payload, and replay writes across transactions or allocate trusted time before exact replay is checked.
- ❌ Do NOT add automatic expiry, cleanup, background work, multiple writers, or payload-bearing diagnostics.

## Approach
Implement the explicit owner-attributed idempotent Retain slice over the ephemeral Generate path and one atomic store transaction.
- Constraint: Reuse GenerateInsightReportQuery and InsightsIdempotencyExecutor; duplicate analytical pipelines are forbidden.
- Expected output: RetainInsightReportCommand
- Expected output: Atomic retained-generation tests

## Interfaces
- Consumes: GenerateInsightReportQuery.HandleAsync (DM-INSIGHTS-INSIGHT-REPORT) — one internally generated complete report

title: Establish CLASSIFY durable state
description:
## Objective
CLASSIFY has one separate owner-only SQLite state store whose immutable history and guarded transitions support every later slice.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-STATE-RETENTION-CLEANUP: Retain attributable state and clean derived artifacts
  - AC: Given an activated rule, apply result, or feedback record, when retention is inspected, then CLASSIFY retains the minimal actor, reason, timestamp, stable references, fingerprints, prior state, and resulting state required for explanation and replay.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path succeeds, when its result is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path returns an expected failure, when its result is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given a validation or evaluation path returns an unexpected handled failure, when its failure is returned, then raw corpus copies and temporary evidence-derived artifacts are absent.
  - AC: Given an unreferenced draft rule, validation run, or evaluation run, when the owner explicitly abandons it, then it becomes non-activatable and its removable derived payload is deleted without changing active rules or LEDGER.
  - AC: Given a rule version, evaluation, or apply result referenced by active state, Ledger mutation provenance, or feedback, when hard removal is requested, then CLASSIFY rejects removal and requires lifecycle retirement or retained history.
  - AC: Given process startup, when orphan temporary artifacts from a prior crash are found, then CLASSIFY validates ownership and removes only recognized CLASSIFY temporaries before accepting new mutation.
  - AC: Given cleanup completion, when status is requested, then it returns cleanup run ID, policy version, removed artifact count, retained artifact count, and per-kind counts but no removed payload or path.

## Depends On
- None; this is an initial ready-frontier bead.

## In Scope
Create the owner-only raw-SQLite store, full designed schema, guarded migrations, row mapping, and operation idempotency foundation.

- ClassifyStateStore
- ClassifySchema migration chain
- ClassifyOperationIdempotencyStore
- ClassifyRowMapper

- Define the canonical idempotency request fingerprint and persistence contract used by every CLASSIFY mutation and operation replay.

## Out of Scope
- bd-3hcn (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-ABANDON-CLEANUP) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- bd-2fdz (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-PRIVATE-CORPUS-READER) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- bd-1qb6 (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-RULE-DRAFT-SAVE) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- Do not modify files reserved by sibling beads or implement any capability outside the twelve-operation CLASSIFY v1 surface.

## Success Criteria
- On linux-x64 the CLASSIFY directory is 0700 and database, WAL, SHM, lock, report, and temporary files are 0600; unsupported ownership or permissions block persistence.
- Startup applies ordered user_version migrations with foreign_keys ON, WAL, synchronous FULL, bounded busy handling, and a single supported owner writer.
- Rule, validation, evaluation, apply, feedback, abandonment, cleanup, and operation-idempotency tables match the nine CLASSIFY data-model contracts.
- Immutable versions, outcomes, terminal item results, feedback, and lifecycle rows reject UPDATE and DELETE; guarded transitions require the expected prior state.
- Reusing an idempotency key with the same request returns the stored result; a different request returns a stable conflict.

- For an idempotency key, the stored fingerprint is SHA-256 over canonical UTF-8 JSON of `operation_id`, `contract_version`, actor kind/label/run ID, and normalized request input; object keys are sorted, null handling is explicit, volatile timestamps are excluded, and the idempotency key itself is not part of the compared request tuple.
- Reusing a key with the identical tuple returns the byte-identical stored result; reusing it with any different operation, contract version, actor, or input returns the stable conflict before handler effects or state mutation.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do not share the Ledger database, use flat JSON, add a hosted database, or use EF Core/DbContext - rejected by DD-CLASSIFY-STATE-STORE.
- ❌ Do not introduce generic repositories, provider-neutral units of work, or speculative storage interfaces - rejected by DD-CLASSIFY-APPLICATION-ARCHITECTURE.
- ❌ Do not persist raw corpus rows or full Ledger projection payloads.
- ❌ Do not permit implicit cascade deletion of referenced history - per ADR-CORE-0020.

- ❌ Do not compare raw JSON text without canonicalization, omit actor/operation/version from the fingerprint, include volatile timestamps, or allow a mismatched replay to execute a handler.

## Approach
Create the owner-only raw-SQLite store, full designed schema, guarded migrations, row mapping, and operation idempotency foundation.

Constraints:
- Use Microsoft.Data.Sqlite and explicit caller-owned transactions; SQL behavior is verified with real temporary stores.

Expected outputs:
- ClassifyStateStore
- ClassifySchema migration chain
- ClassifyOperationIdempotencyStore
- ClassifyRowMapper

- Persist the idempotency key, canonical request fingerprint, operation/version identity, and stored process result atomically. The replay path compares the canonical tuple before invoking any handler and returns the original serialized result on an exact match.

## Interfaces
- Produces: ClassifyStateStore (DM-CLASSIFY-STATE-STORE)
- Produces: ClassifyOperationIdempotencyStore (DM-CLASSIFY-STATE-STORE)
- Produces: ClassifyRowMapper (DM-CLASSIFY-STATE-STORE)

- **Test:** `dotnet test tests/Tally.Tests/Tally.Tests.csproj --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~ClassifyStateStoreTests|FullyQualifiedName~ClassifyHistoryInvariantTests'` — exit 0; at least 28 migration, pragma, permission, idempotency, transaction, immutability, and guarded-transition cases are discovered and 0 fail

title: Verify authorized apply and recovery
description:
## Objective
UC-CLASSIFY-003 proves all-or-none preflight, explicit authority, at-most-once Ledger mutation, and an exact recoverable per-item frontier.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-APPLY-AUTHORIZATION: Authorize a Classification Apply Run
  - AC: Given any suggestion, when evaluation completes without an explicit apply invocation, then no LEDGER mutation occurs.
  - AC: Given selected current suggestions, when apply preview is requested, then the preview identifies the evaluation and fingerprint, target category, rule versions, selected transaction identities, selection count, exclusions, no-suggestion count, and conflict count.
  - AC: Given selected current suggestions, when apply preview is requested, then the preview operation performs no LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given an exact rule without explicit owner-approved broad-apply authority, when rule-wide apply is requested, then CLASSIFY rejects the request before LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given an exact rule with explicit owner-approved broad-apply authority, when the owner explicitly requests apply for its current preview, then only current unambiguous suggestions produced by that exact rule are authorized.
  - AC: Given a no-suggestion, conflict, or stale outcome, when apply preview is built, then that outcome is excluded from the authorized selection.
  - AC: Given any fingerprint change after preview, when apply is requested, then CLASSIFY rejects the preview as stale before LEDGER mutation.
- FR-CLASSIFY-APPLY-EXECUTION: Apply authorized decisions through public LEDGER operations
  - AC: Given an authorized selection whose evaluation, projection, category, normalization, and rule-set fingerprints are current, when apply starts, then CLASSIFY completes preflight before the first LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given any stale or incompatible item detected during preflight, when apply starts, then CLASSIFY rejects the whole requested selection before the first LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given an authorized uncategorized active transaction and active category, when its item is submitted, then CLASSIFY invokes only the public LEDGER category-assignment operation with a stable per-transaction idempotency identity.
  - AC: Given an already categorized transaction, when a correction is explicitly selected, then CLASSIFY requires a transaction-specific owner reason and never includes that correction in exact-rule broad apply.
  - AC: Given an apply request, when processing terminates, then every requested transaction has one structured result of applied, already-applied, rejected, failed, or unresolved.
  - AC: Given the same apply identity and semantically identical request, when apply is retried, then CLASSIFY returns the prior terminal item results and creates no second category mutation.
  - AC: Given an apply identity reused with different selection, category, mode, fingerprint, or reason, when apply is retried, then CLASSIFY returns a stable conflict and preserves the original results.
  - AC: Given interruption between item submissions, when the same apply run is resumed, then completed items reconcile from durable results and processing continues only from the exact unresolved frontier.
- FR-CLASSIFY-OUTCOME-INVALIDATION: Invalidate Stale Classification Outcomes
  - AC: Given a transaction becomes void in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a transaction is superseded in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a transaction allocation changes in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a transaction's transfer relationship changes in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a transaction's refund or reversal relationship changes in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a targeted category is archived, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a targeted category is reactivated, when a prior outcome created before reactivation is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a targeted category identity changes, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a category rename that preserves the same active identifier, when a prior outcome is inspected, then its category identity remains valid and the current display name is returned.
  - AC: Given the required LEDGER contract or classification projection version changes, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY identifies that changed fingerprint dimension and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given the LEDGER store generation changes, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY identifies that changed fingerprint dimension and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given the source LEDGER snapshot is invalid or expired, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY identifies that changed fingerprint dimension and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given the normalization version changes, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY identifies that changed fingerprint dimension and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given the active Rule Set Version changes, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY identifies that changed fingerprint dimension and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a stale outcome, when the owner requests the permitted next operation, then CLASSIFY returns re-evaluate and does not return correction or apply.

## Depends On
- bd-gv0z (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-APPLY-PREVIEW): UC-003 verifies preview and run as one published authorized-apply workflow.
- bd-2ffc (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-APPLY-RUN-SAGA): The UC verifies the complete preview and apply saga.
- bd-3g6y (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-INT-PUBLIC-CONTRACT): Acceptance invokes the published process boundary.

## In Scope

- VerifiedClassifyUc003

## Out of Scope

- Do not modify files reserved by sibling beads or implement any capability outside the twelve-operation CLASSIFY v1 surface.

## Success Criteria
- Evaluation alone mutates no Ledger state; current preview is exact and read-only.
- Stale selection rejects wholly before mutation; conflict and no-suggestion never enter scope.
- Uncategorized assignment and one explicitly reasoned correction use public Ledger operations and broad mode never includes correction.
- Every item returns applied, already_applied, rejected, failed, or unresolved; identical replay creates no second allocation.
- Every interruption resumes only the durable unresolved frontier and conflicting identity reuse preserves original results.

## Failure Criteria

- ❌ Do not treat aggregate run success as proof of per-item exactness or duplicate prevention.

title: Define deterministic unresolved grouping policy
description:
## Objective
Produce bounded repeat-pattern aggregates with checked arithmetic and drift fingerprints without persistence or rule authority.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-UNRESOLVED-PATTERN-REPORT: Report repeated unresolved classification patterns

## Depends On
- None; this bead is an intended ready-root task.

## In Scope
Only the outcome, interfaces, and exact reservation globs named in this bead. Preserve all unchanged released contracts and repository conventions.

## Out of Scope
Do not access SQLite or Ledger, persist descriptions, or create rules; bd-3ciw owns the fresh-join query and ephemeral owner-visible result.

## Success Criteria
- The group key is normalizationVersion, normalizedDescription, accountId, and amountDirection using ordinal equality; counts and signed/absolute minor-unit totals use checked arithmetic.
- Ordering is count descending, then normalizedDescription, accountId, and direction ordinal; topN accepts 1 through 500 and identical inputs yield identical group fingerprints.
- The pure result exposes owner-visible normalized description and aggregates but contains no transaction IDs, source paths, rule proposal, activation, feedback, or durable artifact instruction.
- Overflow, over-limit, empty normalization version, invalid direction, and impossible row accounting return typed failures with no partial groups.

## Failure Criteria
- Do not add fuzzy clustering, merchant inference, regex, token persistence, priority, rule creation, or model scoring.
- Do not log group descriptions, amounts, account IDs, or input rows from the policy.

## Approach
Implement the pure grouping, ordering, top-N, fingerprint, and disclosure policy for owner-visible unresolved review.

Expected outputs:
- UnresolvedPatternGroupingPolicy and canonical group fingerprint vectors

Constraints:
- The policy is pure, deterministic, bounded, and independent of storage or Ledger access.

## Interfaces
- UnresolvedPatternGroupingPolicy (produces) - DM-CLASSIFY-UNRESOLVED-REPORT - ordered bounded groups

title: Authorize exact apply previews
description:
## Objective
The owner receives an expiry-bound read-only preview containing only current explicitly authorized assignment or correction items.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-APPLY-AUTHORIZATION: Authorize a Classification Apply Run
  - AC: Given any suggestion, when evaluation completes without an explicit apply invocation, then no LEDGER mutation occurs.
  - AC: Given selected current suggestions, when apply preview is requested, then the preview identifies the evaluation and fingerprint, target category, rule versions, selected transaction identities, selection count, exclusions, no-suggestion count, and conflict count.
  - AC: Given selected current suggestions, when apply preview is requested, then the preview operation performs no LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given an exact rule without explicit owner-approved broad-apply authority, when rule-wide apply is requested, then CLASSIFY rejects the request before LEDGER mutation.
  - AC: Given an exact rule with explicit owner-approved broad-apply authority, when the owner explicitly requests apply for its current preview, then only current unambiguous suggestions produced by that exact rule are authorized.
  - AC: Given a no-suggestion, conflict, or stale outcome, when apply preview is built, then that outcome is excluded from the authorized selection.
  - AC: Given any fingerprint change after preview, when apply is requested, then CLASSIFY rejects the preview as stale before LEDGER mutation.
- FR-CLASSIFY-OUTCOME-INVALIDATION: Invalidate Stale Classification Outcomes
  - AC: Given a transaction becomes void in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a transaction is superseded in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a transaction allocation changes in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a transaction's transfer relationship changes in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.

title: Verify replay and overlap safety workflow
description:
## Objective

Prove repeated or overlapping statements never create an unjustified duplicate suppression or second canonical transaction.

## Implements

- No direct FR; this task is a prerequisite or verification gate.

## Depends On

- bd-2jn (TASK-INGEST-GATE-INT-PUBLIC-CONTRACT): UC verification exercises the complete published preview/commit/status contract.

## In Scope

- UCIngest004Evidence

## Out of Scope

- Do NOT alter private fixtures or tracked expectations to manufacture identity evidence.
- Do NOT inspect internal hashes/stores; use public preview/status/receipt and Ledger observations.

## Success Criteria

- The same Source Fingerprint, selected account, adapter version, and LEDGER contract version under any filename returns the prior active or completed batch or receipt before reparsing and creates no new Ledger effect; changing any key component requires a new preview.
- A familiar filename with changed bytes is a new preview, never Exact Replay.
- Identical date-description-amount rows at distinct source positions remain separate candidates; tuple equality never collapses them.
- Only variant-proven exact identity with equal immutable facts may be Exact Duplicate; unavailable/incompatible provenance never claims automatic deduplication.
- An exact identity reused with changed immutable facts returns stable conflict and preserves the original transaction.
- A different source with an overlapping account/date window and no cross-file identity returns blocking Overlap Conflict and remains uncommitted.

## Failure Criteria

- ❌ Do NOT alter private fixtures or tracked expectations to manufacture identity evidence.
- ❌ Do NOT inspect internal hashes/stores; use public preview/status/receipt and Ledger observations.

title: Calculate exact Analysis Window and category metrics
description:
## Objective
ExactMetricCalculator accounts for every member exactly once and returns reconciled signed ZAR metrics for each requested window.

## Implements
- FR-INSIGHTS-EXACT-WINDOW-METRICS: Calculate exact Analysis Window metrics
  - AC: Given a complete coherent evidence set, when exact metrics are calculated, then one total actual metric is returned for each requested day, week, and month-to-date window.
  - AC: Given a requested category breakdown, when exact metrics are calculated, then every stable category present in plan or actual evidence is accounted for in deterministic category-identity order.
  - AC: Given plan entries with zero amount, actual categories omitted from the plan, or uncategorized actuals, when metrics are returned, then Zero Budget, Unbudgeted, and Uncategorized remain distinct explicit buckets.
  - AC: Given refunds or reversals that make a window or category net actual negative, when metrics are returned, then the signed exact value is preserved and is not clamped to zero.
  - AC: Given no matching recorded actuals in a started window, when metrics are returned, then the exact value is zero with a successful evidence state rather than Not Found.
  - AC: Given no Budget Plan, when exact actual metrics are available, then they are returned with No Budget Plan on every plan-relative field.
  - AC: Given exact category and bucket values, when totals are returned, then total actual equals the checked exact sum of Budgeted, Zero Budget, Unbudgeted, and Uncategorized values.
  - AC: Given any Int64 overflow, undefined exact operation, or reconciliation failure, when metrics are calculated, then the entire report fails with no partial financial output.

## Depends On
- bd-1qz (TASK-INSIGHTS-CONTRACT-MODELS): The calculator consumes evidence and produces exact analytical contracts.

## In Scope
- Make one deterministic checked pass over complete dated members for total, category, and bucket metrics.
- Produce: ExactMetricCalculator
- Produce: Exact arithmetic property matrix

## Out of Scope
- No sibling handoff beyond the explicit Depends On and Failure Criteria contracts.

## Success Criteria
- Each requested started day, week, and month-to-date window returns one exact total and, when requested, categories in stable identity order.
- Budgeted, ZeroBudget, Unbudgeted, and Uncategorized are distinct; NoBudgetPlan preserves exact actuals with NoBudgetPlan on plan-relative fields.
- Signed refunds and reversals remain negative, an empty matching set returns exact zero, and total actual equals the checked exact sum of all buckets.
- Every member contributes exactly once per applicable metric; duplicate accounting, overflow, undefined exact operation, or reconciliation mismatch aborts the whole report.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do NOT use floating point, clamp refunds to zero, suppress zero results, merge Uncategorized with Unbudgeted, or invent a plan.
- ❌ Do NOT expose per-metric public services or move orchestration to callers — rejected per DD-INSIGHTS-DETERMINISTIC-REPORT-COMPILER.
- ❌ Do NOT emit partial metric collections after arithmetic or reconciliation failure.

## Approach
Make one deterministic checked pass over complete dated members for total, category, and bucket metrics.
- Constraint: Use checked Int64 minor units and deterministic catalogue/category order.
- Expected output: ExactMetricCalculator
- Expected output: Exact arithmetic property matrix

## Interfaces
- Consumes: BoundInsightEvidence (DM-INSIGHTS-COHERENT-EVIDENCE) — complete validated dated members
- Produces: ExactMetricCalculator.Calculate (DM-INSIGHTS-ANALYTICAL-EVIDENCE) — ordered exact MetricResult collection

title: Carry frozen Spend Category ancestry from the LEDGER snapshot into BUDGET members
description:
## Objective
Every materialized Budget Actual member carries the frozen Spend Category ancestry from the cited LEDGER actuals snapshot, and every ancestry identifier resolves in the known Spend Category evidence set.

## Implements
- FR-BUDGET-LEDGER-COMPOSITION: Compose only through public LEDGER contracts
  - AC: Given a Budget Position request, when BUDGET obtains actuals, then it requests Budget Actual values for the exact Budget Period and current category and categorization state under one cited LEDGER snapshot.
  - AC: Given LEDGER returns transfer, refund, correction, allocation, void, supersession, or lifecycle-aware Budget Actual values, when BUDGET consumes them, then those values are used verbatim and no financial transaction is reclassified or reinterpreted.
  - AC: Given LEDGER actuals require multiple pages, when BUDGET completes the query, then every page belongs to the same snapshot and every returned member is accounted for exactly once.

## Depends On
- bd-1xlf (TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-CONTRACTS): The mapper assigns BudgetActualMember.AncestryIds, which that bead adds to the record.

## In Scope
- BudgetContractMapper.TryMapActualMembers carries item.FrozenAncestryIds into AncestryIds
- GetBudgetPositionQuery adds every ancestry identifier to the required Spend Category identifier set

## Out of Scope
- Declaring the AncestryIds field — bd-1xlf (TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-CONTRACTS)
- Resolving an envelope from the ancestry — bd-3uzt (TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-RESOLUTION)

## Success Criteria
- Given a LEDGER actuals snapshot whose items carry FrozenAncestryIds, when BudgetContractMapper.TryMapActualMembers runs, then each produced BudgetActualMember carries that same ancestry list in the same order rather than an empty list.
- Given a LEDGER actuals item with no assigned Spend Category, when the member is mapped, then its AncestryIds list is empty and its CategoryId is null.
- Given a Budget Actual assigned to a Spend Category whose ancestor is archived and absent from the default category listing, when the position query assembles known Spend Category evidence, then that ancestor identifier is fetched and present so ancestry validation does not fail.
- Given a Budget Position request, when the required Spend Category identifier set is assembled, then it contains every plan entry category, every member category, and every ancestry element.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do NOT reach into LEDGER private storage or recompute ancestry inside BUDGET — consume ancestry only from the public actuals snapshot, per DD-BUDGET-LEDGER-PUBLIC-COMPOSITION.
- ❌ Do NOT issue one LEDGER actuals query per Category Budget Entry using the categoryScope subtree filter — rejected alternative B in DD-BUDGET-CATEGORY-ENVELOPE-RESOLUTION, because nested entries return overlapping membership and it breaks the single-complete-snapshot rule.
- ❌ Do NOT resolve, bucket, or aggregate anything in this task — TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-RESOLUTION owns resolution.

## Approach
- One complete compatible actuals snapshot per position; no additional LEDGER actuals query is introduced.
- CancellationToken flows through every added async call.

Expected outputs:
- Mapper that carries FrozenAncestryIds into BudgetActualMember.AncestryIds
- Required Spend Category identifier set extended with every ancestry element

## Interfaces
- Consumes: BudgetActualMember.AncestryIds (DM-BUDGET-POSITION-PROJECTION) — Field published by TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-CONTRACTS
- Produces: BudgetContractMapper.TryMapActualMembers (DM-BUDGET-LEDGER-COMPOSITION-CONTRACT)

title: Publish the eleven-operation INSIGHTS contract foundation
description:
## Objective
The shared registry can describe every Public INSIGHTS Operation and policy without reading financial or retained data.

## Implements
- FR-INSIGHTS-CONTRACT-DISCOVERY: Discover the Public INSIGHTS Operation contract
  - AC: Given a compatible caller with no financial input, when operation discovery is requested, then every Public INSIGHTS Operation is returned in canonical verb order with stable operation identity and contract version.
  - AC: Given one discovered operation, when its descriptor is inspected, then request and result schema fingerprints, mutability, authority, idempotency requirement, limits, stable error types, exit categories, and compatibility range are explicit.
  - AC: Given policy discovery, when the catalogue is returned, then every released Analysis Window, formula, Evidence Sufficiency, severity, explanation, and ordering policy has stable kind, version, status, and fingerprint metadata.
  - AC: Given a formally deferred Forecast, Trend, Anomaly, or Attention Item policy, when policy discovery is requested, then it is marked unsupported and no executable formula or threshold is advertised.
  - AC: Given INSIGHTS authority metadata, when it is inspected, then no LEDGER, CLASSIFY, or BUDGET mutation operation is present.
  - AC: Given an unsupported INSIGHTS contract version, when discovery is requested, then one stable compatibility failure is returned without reading financial data.
  - AC: Given discovery, help, or schema output, when all fields are inspected, then no report payload, amount, merchant text, private path, permission seed, role template, menu seed, translation key, or frontend key model is present.
- FR-INSIGHTS-STRUCTURED-INVOCATION: Invoke Public INSIGHTS Operations non-interactively
  - AC: Given valid structured input through stdin or an approved owner-only file, when a public operation succeeds, then exactly one versioned structured business-result envelope is written to stdout and the process exits with the documented success category.
  - AC: Given an expected validation, Not Found, Deleted, conflict, unavailable, insufficient-evidence, compatibility, integrity, resource, or downstream failure, when invocation completes, then exactly one module-scoped machine-readable error or state envelope is returned with the documented exit category.
  - AC: Given malformed input or a schema-forbidden unknown field, when invocation is attempted, then validation fails before any financial read or retained-state write.
  - AC: Given an unsupported INSIGHTS, BUDGET, or LEDGER contract version, when invocation is attempted, then compatibility fails before financial processing.
  - AC: Given Retain, Restate, Delete, Backup, or Restore without required P1 actor attribution or idempotency identity, when invocation is attempted, then authority validation fails before retained-state change.
  - AC: Given any operation, when it runs, then it requires no interactive prompt, network call, daemon, watcher, scheduler, service, or background Tally process.
  - AC: Given success or expected failure, when stderr, logs, telemetry, crash output, process arguments, and shared temporary locations are inspected, then they contain metadata only and no serialized financial request, report, or response body.

## Depends On
- bd-1qz (TASK-INSIGHTS-CONTRACT-MODELS): Requests, results, JSON metadata, descriptors, and mapper reference the analytical and lifecycle contract records.
- bd-21u (TASK-INSIGHTS-LIFECYCLE-CONTRACT-MODELS): The eleven public operations include retained-history recovery status and private-receipt contract types.

## In Scope
- Create versioned requests, results, stable errors, source-generated JSON metadata, eleven descriptors, and the pure contract mapper over the shared Tally operation abstractions.
- Produce: InsightsOperationModule

- Produce: InsightsContractMapper

## Out of Scope
- Public-contract gate owns registration and Program wiring.

## Success Criteria
- InsightsOperationModule contains exactly insights.report.generate, insights.report.explain, insights.report.get, insights.report.list, insights.report.retain, insights.report.restate, insights.report.delete, insights.status.get, insights.backup.create, insights.backup.verify, and insights.restore.activate in canonical verb order; Discover remains shared system.schema.list/show.
- Every descriptor publishes deterministic request/result fingerprints, compatibility range, authority, mutability, idempotency requirement, released limits, stable errors, and exit categories without reading a store or producer.
- Retain, Restate, Delete, Backup, and Restore require actor attribution and idempotency; Generate, Explain, Get, List, Status, and Verify are read-only; unsupported versions and unknown fields fail before financial reads.
- Complex input is accepted only through stdin or an approved owner-only file boundary, exactly one business envelope uses stdout, and diagnostics are metadata-only.
- The released policy catalogue marks Forecast, Trend, Anomaly, and Attention Item as Deferred and exposes no executable formula, threshold, severity, or mutation operation for them.

title: Explain and invalidate retained outcomes
description:
## Objective
The owner can reproduce a retained outcome or learn exactly why it is stale without reconstruction, unrelated data, or forced apply.

## Implements
- FR-CLASSIFY-OUTCOME-EXPLANATION: Explain a classification outcome
  - AC: Given a retained suggestion, when its explanation is requested, then the result identifies the evaluation, transaction, category, normalization version, Rule Set Version, contributing rule versions, and allowed fields whose predicates matched.
  - AC: Given a retained no-suggestion outcome, when its explanation is requested, then the result identifies the evaluated versions and a stable no-match reason without inventing a category.
  - AC: Given a retained conflict, when its explanation is requested, then the result identifies every incompatible matching rule version and proposed category without selecting a winner.
  - AC: Given a stale outcome, when its explanation is requested, then the result identifies the fingerprint dimension that changed and states that re-evaluation is required.
  - AC: Given an unknown outcome, when explanation is requested, then CLASSIFY returns stable not-found status and does not reconstruct historical evidence from current state.
  - AC: Given a known outcome whose retained evidence is unavailable, when explanation is requested, then CLASSIFY returns stable evidence-unavailable status and does not reconstruct historical evidence from current state.
- FR-CLASSIFY-OUTCOME-INVALIDATION: Invalidate Stale Classification Outcomes
  - AC: Given a transaction becomes void in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a transaction is superseded in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a transaction allocation changes in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a transaction's transfer relationship changes in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a transaction's refund or reversal relationship changes in public LEDGER state, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a targeted category is archived, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a targeted category is reactivated, when a prior outcome created before reactivation is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a targeted category identity changes, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY reports it stale and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a category rename that preserves the same active identifier, when a prior outcome is inspected, then its category identity remains valid and the current display name is returned.
  - AC: Given the required LEDGER contract or classification projection version changes, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY identifies that changed fingerprint dimension and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given the LEDGER store generation changes, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY identifies that changed fingerprint dimension and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given the source LEDGER snapshot is invalid or expired, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY identifies that changed fingerprint dimension and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given the normalization version changes, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY identifies that changed fingerprint dimension and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given the active Rule Set Version changes, when a prior outcome is inspected or applied, then CLASSIFY identifies that changed fingerprint dimension and blocks apply.
  - AC: Given a stale outcome, when the owner requests the permitted next operation, then CLASSIFY returns re-evaluate and does not return correction or apply.

## Depends On
- bd-8uew (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-EVALUATION-WORKFLOW): Outcome inspection reads the retained evaluation and evidence produced by this task.
- bd-2olb (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-LEDGER-CLASSIFICATION-CLIENT): Consumes an interface produced by TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-LEDGER-CLASSIFICATION-CLIENT.

## In Scope
Implement outcome.get with bounded historical evidence, current display names, complete fingerprint staleness, and one permitted next-operation enum value.

- GetClassificationOutcomeQuery
- ClassificationStalenessPolicy
- Bounded outcome result mapping

## Out of Scope
- bd-gv0z (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-APPLY-PREVIEW) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- bd-3g6y (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-GATE-INT-PUBLIC-CONTRACT) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- bd-3cp2 (TASK-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-VERIFY-UC-002) owns its dependent integration and verification slice.
- Do not modify files reserved by sibling beads or implement any capability outside the twelve-operation CLASSIFY v1 surface.

## Success Criteria
- Suggestion, no-suggestion, and conflict explanations return exact retained evaluation, transaction, category, normalization, rule-set, contributing rules, allowed matched fields, and stable reason without unrelated payloads.
- Unknown outcome and known outcome with unavailable retained evidence return distinct stable statuses and never reconstruct evidence from current state.
- Transaction, allocation, transfer, refund, category lifecycle, contract, projection, store generation, snapshot, normalization, and rule-set changes each name the changed fingerprint dimension and allow only re-evaluation.
- A same-identifier active category rename preserves validity and returns the current display name; archive or reactivation stales the outcome.
- Stale, conflict, and no-suggestion outcomes remain unappliable.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do not reconstruct missing MatchEvidence from current Ledger or rule state - rejected by DD-CLASSIFY-DETERMINISTIC-EVALUATION.
- ❌ Do not treat display-name rename as category identity change.
- ❌ Do not expose raw descriptions, normalized values, corpus rows, hidden rule payloads, or full requests.

title: Prove envelope provenance and reparent re-lensing through the published contract
description:
## Objective
The published BUDGET operations report the effective Spend Category per Budget Actual and re-lens a later position after a reparent under a newly cited snapshot, with the full existing position suite unchanged.

## Implements
- FR-BUDGET-INSIGHTS-PROJECTION: Expose a read-only INSIGHTS projection
  - AC: Given a version-compatible INSIGHTS consumer, when it requests plan or position data, then BUDGET returns the same exact domain result and provenance available through the owner read contract.
- FR-BUDGET-POSITION-QUERY: Calculate exact Budget Positions
  - AC: Given a Budget Plan Revision whose Spend Categories are all root nodes with no descendants, when the position is calculated, then every value, bucket, ordering, and total is identical to the `budget-position-v1` exact-identity result for the same inputs.
  - AC: Given a successful position over a hierarchical Spend Category tree, when a Budget Actual member is inspected through the INSIGHTS read projection, then it reports its frozen Spend Category ancestry root-first with the assigned Spend Category last, and reports the effective Spend Category identifier that governed it, or null when the outcome is Unbudgeted Spend or Uncategorized Spend.

## Depends On
- bd-3uzt (TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-RESOLUTION): The gate proves resolution behavior through the published contract and cannot pass before resolution exists.
- bd-113k (TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-INTEGRITY): Integrity behaviour is proven by bd-113k; this bead uses targeted provenance tests plus the fast Budget verify script.

## In Scope
- Per-member envelope provenance proven through budget.insights.evidence.get on the published binary
- Reparent re-lensing proven end to end with two differing cited snapshot identifiers
- The complete existing 111-test position suite run unchanged

## Out of Scope
- Implementing resolution — bd-3uzt (TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-RESOLUTION)
- Implementing integrity validation — bd-113k (TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-INTEGRITY)

## Success Criteria
- Given Budget Actuals across a depth-three Spend Category tree with Category Budget Entries on the root and one descendant, when budget.insights.evidence.get is invoked through the published binary, then each member reports its frozen ancestry root-first with its assigned Spend Category last and reports the effective Spend Category identifier that governed it.
- Given a member resolving to Unbudgeted Spend or Uncategorized Spend, when the INSIGHTS read projection is inspected, then its effective Spend Category identifier is null rather than an invented ancestor.
- Given a Budget Actual on a descendant under a funded parent, when the descendant is reparented under a different funded Spend Category through ledger.category.reparent and the position is requested again for the same Budget Period and revision, then the Budget Actual is attributed to the new funded ancestor, the cited LEDGER snapshot identifier differs from the first read, and the bound revision identifier and status are unchanged.
- Given the complete existing position test suite, when it is run after resolution lands, then all 111 tests pass with no test modified to accommodate the new behavior.

## Failure Criteria
- ❌ Do NOT modify an existing position test to make it pass under the new rule — unchanged flat-taxonomy behavior is the regression proof, per DD-BUDGET-CATEGORY-ENVELOPE-RESOLUTION.
- ❌ Do NOT assert that a historical position is immutable across a reparent — determinism holds within one cited snapshot, not across time, per DD-BUDGET-CATEGORY-ENVELOPE-RESOLUTION and A4.
- ❌ Do NOT exercise the behavior through in-process calculator calls only — this gate proves the published operation contract.

## Approach
- Tests drive the published Native AOT binary through TALLY_PUBLISHED_BINARY, matching the existing BUDGET contract-test harness.
- TALLY_DATA_ROOT points at a temporary owner-only directory per test.

Expected outputs:
- Contract-level proof of per-member envelope provenance
- End-to-end proof that a reparent re-lenses a later position under a new snapshot
- Green full existing position suite

## Interfaces
- Consumes: BudgetPositionCalculator.ResolveEnvelope (DM-BUDGET-POSITION-PROJECTION) — Resolution produced by TASK-BUDGET-ENVELOPE-RESOLUTION

## Files (reservation globs)
- `tests/Tally.Tests/Budget/InsightsContract/BudgetInsightsContractTests.cs` (modify)
- `tests/Tally.Tests/Budget/Acceptance/BudgetEnvelopeProvenanceTests.cs` (create)
- `tests/Tally.Tests/Budget/Acceptance/BudgetUc003PositionTests.cs` (read)

## Verification
- **Build:** `dotnet build Tally.slnx --nologo` — Build succeeded with 0 errors and 0 warnings
- **Test:** `dotnet test tests/Tally.Tests/Tally.Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~BudgetEnvelopeProvenanceTests` — All BudgetEnvelopeProvenanceTests pass, exit code 0, at least 3 tests run
- **Test:** `dotnet test tests/Tally.Tests/Tally.Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~BudgetUc003PositionTests` — All BudgetUc003PositionTests pass unchanged, exit code 0, at least 31 tests run
- **Test:** `bash scripts/verify-budget-fast.sh` — Script exits 0 within hard wall-clock limit; core envelope suites discovered and green (module ship gate is TASK-BUDGET-GATE-MODULE only)

## Commit
